};

## CheckpointWhen  chord/src/documents/definition.ts
used by: chord-effect via StateDefinition
/** Whether a commit's change of a persisted document is stored as a whole new base (`true`) or as a delta. */
export type CheckpointWhen<T> = (value: T, ops: readonly Op[], info: CheckpointInfo) => boolean;

## CommitPersistence  chord/src/documents/definition.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * When a commit reaches the store (Durable's `CommitPersistence`): `immediate`, the default, before the commit
 * resolves; `deferred` (a persisted run's state change, D8): adopted and published at once, stored with the next
 * immediate change, the run's outcome, the object's close, or about `withinMs` (default 1,000 ms) later.
 */
export type CommitPersistence =
	| { readonly kind: "immediate" }
	| { readonly kind: "deferred"; readonly withinMs?: number };

## defineState  chord/src/documents/definition.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * Declares a document: a singleton per object, or with `keyed: true` many per object, each by a string key, or with
 * `keyed: <host kind>` many per object, each by an address of that kind, belonging to that host (the store exports,
 * imports and deletes it with the host's data); with `persist: true` stored in the host's store. Its name is a
 * restricted name (lowercase `[a-z0-9@/._~-]`).
 */
export function defineState<S extends Schema, K extends KeyedBy = false>(
	name: string,
	options: StateOptions<S, K> & { readonly persist?: false; readonly checkpointWhen?: never },
): StateDefinition<DocumentOf<S>, K, false>;
export function defineState<S extends Schema, K extends KeyedBy = false>(
	name: string,
	options: StateOptions<S, K> & PersistOptions<S>,
): StateDefinition<DocumentOf<S>, K, true>;
export function defineState<S extends Schema, K extends KeyedBy>(
	name: string,
	options: StateOptions<S, K> & {
		readonly persist?: boolean;
		readonly checkpointWhen?: CheckpointWhen<DocumentOf<S>>;
	},
): StateDefinition<DocumentOf<S>, K, boolean>

## DocumentOf  chord/src/documents/definition.ts
used by: chord-effect via defineState
/** The value of a document whose schema is `S`: its static type, which must be a JSON object. */
type DocumentOf<S extends Schema> = Static<S> extends JsonObject ? Static<S> : never;

## JsonObject  chord/src/documents/definition.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** A document root: a JSON object. */
export type JsonObject = { [key: string]: JsonValue };

## KeyedBy  chord/src/documents/definition.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** What a definition is keyed by: nothing (`false`, a singleton), string keys (`true`) or addresses of a host kind. */
export type KeyedBy = boolean | KindShape;

## PersistOptions  chord/src/documents/definition.ts
used by: chord-effect via defineState
/** What a persisted document adds (slice 6a §10): `checkpointWhen` is required. */
type PersistOptions<S extends Schema> = {
	/** Stored in the host's store; only in `local` types with empty params (P3). */
	readonly persist: true;
	/** Called once per commit per changed document; creations and version changes always store a base. */
	readonly checkpointWhen: CheckpointWhen<DocumentOf<S>>;
};

## StateDefinition  chord/src/documents/definition.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** A declared document; `T` is its value, `K` what it is keyed by, `P` whether it is persisted. */
export class StateDefinition<T extends JsonObject, K extends KeyedBy, P extends boolean = false> {
	readonly name: string
	readonly schema: Schema
	readonly version: number
	/** Whether it is keyed: by string keys or by addresses. */
	readonly keyed: boolean
	/** The host kind whose addresses key it (a declared `hostKind`); `undefined` for string keys and singletons. */
	readonly host: KindShape | undefined
	readonly persist: boolean
	/**
	 * `hash64` of the schema's normal form (descriptions and titles ignored), computed once: the same version with
	 * another fingerprint is a schema changed without a version bump.
	 */
	readonly fingerprint: string
	/** Type only: what the definition is keyed by. */
	declare readonly "~keyed"?: K
	/** Type only: whether the definition is persisted. */
	declare readonly "~persist"?: P
	constructor(
		name: string,
		schema: Schema,
		version: number,
		initial: () => T,
		migrate: ((old: JsonObject, from: number) => T) | undefined,
		keyed: KeyedBy,
		persist: boolean,
		checkpointWhen: CheckpointWhen<T> | undefined,
	)
	/** Whether a persisted document's change is stored as a new base (its `checkpointWhen`); never asked in memory. */
	checkpointWhen(value: T, ops: readonly Op[], info: CheckpointInfo): boolean
	/** A fresh `initial()` value; the first is checked against the schema (counted), later ones are not (R8). */
	initial(context: Context): T
	/**
	 * `old`, a value of version `from`, migrated to this version and checked against the schema once, as it is
	 * produced (R8, counted). Throws without a `migrate` (the access is refused, the data kept) and when the result does
	 * not match.
	 */
	migrate(old: JsonObject, from: number, context: Context): T
}

## StateOptions  chord/src/documents/definition.ts
used by: chord-effect via defineState
/** What `defineState` takes for any document. */
type StateOptions<S extends Schema, K extends KeyedBy> = {
	readonly schema: S;
	readonly version: number;
	readonly initial: () => DocumentOf<S>;
	/** Maps a value of an older version `from` to this version's shape; pure. Required to read older values. */
	readonly migrate?: (old: JsonObject, from: number) => DocumentOf<S>;
	/** `true`: many per object by string key; a host kind: many per object, each keyed by an address of that kind. */
	readonly keyed?: K;
};

## TransactionCancelled  chord/src/documents/documents.ts
used by: chord-effect via HostError
/**
 * A transaction (a document change or retirement, `self.tx`, a job start) that did not commit because the context it
 * was started with ended first: a root whose `fn` settled, a handler or routine whose object ended, a caller that
 * cancelled. `error` is that context's abort reason, naming the scope that ended (decision "Mistakes that wait are
 * reported at once" (e)).
 */
export type TransactionCancelled = {
	readonly kind: "transaction_cancelled";
	readonly object: string;
	readonly error: unknown;
};

## HandleOf  chord/src/documents/handles.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** The handle `self.state(definition)` returns. */
export type HandleOf<D> = D extends StateDefinition<infer T, infer K, boolean>
	? K extends true
		? KeyedHandle<T>
		: K extends KindShape
			? KeyedHandle<T, Address<K>>
			: SingletonHandle<T>
	: never;

## KeyedHandle  chord/src/documents/handles.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * Keyed documents: many per object, by `Key`: a string, or an address of the host kind the definition is keyed by
 * (stored by its key). Not a watchable itself: each key is, through `watch(key)` and `at(key)`; a live collection is a
 * singleton holding it.
 */
export interface KeyedHandle<T extends JsonObject, Key = string> {
	/** The document's value, `undefined` when absent (persisted and not in memory: loaded on the object's line). */
	get(key: Key, context: Context): Promise<T | undefined>;
	/** The keys of the present documents, in code point order of their stored keys. */
	keys(context: Context): AsyncIterable<Key>;
	/**
	 * A watch of the document at `key`, `undefined` when absent. It follows the address: a retirement is one frame with
	 * `retired: true` and `initial()`, a later creation a root replacement; it ends with the object.
	 */
	watch(key: Key, context: Context): Promise<WatchHandle<T> | undefined>;
	/**
	 * In the factory only: the document at `key` as a watchable (a state member, a derive source, an `on` source),
	 * `initial()` while absent, loaded before the object goes live and pinned while this attempt lives.
	 */
	at(key: Key): Watchable<T>;
	/** One transaction that drafts the document at `key` and passes the draft to `fn`. */
	change<R>(key: Key, fn: (draft: Draft<T>) => R, context: Context): Promise<R>;
	/** One transaction that retires the document at `key` (a no-op when absent). */
	retire(key: Key, context: Context): Promise<void>;
}

## SingletonHandle  chord/src/documents/handles.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** A singleton document: a watchable that always has a value (`initial()` until written, and after a retire). */
export interface SingletonHandle<T extends JsonObject> extends Watchable<T> {
	/** One transaction that drafts this document and passes the draft to `fn`. */
	change<R>(fn: (draft: Draft<T>) => R, context: Context): Promise<R>;
	/** One transaction that retires this document: back to `initial()`. */
	retire(context: Context): Promise<void>;
}

## Tx  chord/src/documents/transaction.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** What `self.tx` gives its callback. Inside it: only `await tx.*`, no other `self.tx`, no calls to other objects. */
export interface Tx {
	/** The document's draft: the same one for the same document within one transaction. */
	draft<T extends JsonObject>(handle: SingletonHandle<T>): Promise<Draft<T>>;
	draft<T extends JsonObject, Key>(handle: KeyedHandle<T, Key>, key: NoInfer<Key>): Promise<Draft<T>>;
	/** Retires the document when the transaction commits (its address reads `initial()` again); a no-op when it is absent. */
	retire(handle: SingletonHandle<JsonObject>): Promise<void>;
	retire<Key>(handle: KeyedHandle<JsonObject, Key>, key: NoInfer<Key>): Promise<void>;
	/**
	 * Starts a run of `job`, one of this object's jobs, with this transaction's other writes (§15): both commit or
	 * neither. Returns its `Run` at once; a discarded transaction's `Run` rejects `released` from `outcome`. A key of an
	 * unsettled run (one started earlier in this transaction too) returns that run.
	 */
	start<A, R, S>(job: JobHandle<A, R, S>, args: A, options?: StartOptions): Run<Outcome<A, R, S>>;
	/** The row with `key` as this transaction leaves it (its own `put`, `update`, `delete` overlaid; W10). */
	get<C extends Columns, K extends readonly string[]>(
		table: Table<C, K>,
		key: KeyOf<C, K>,
	): Promise<RowOf<C> | undefined>;
	/** A page of committed rows, stable for the transaction (without its own writes). */
	page<C extends Columns, K extends readonly string[]>(
		table: Table<C, K>,
		q: Query<C, K>,
		limit: number,
		options?: PageOptions,
	): Promise<Page<RowOf<C>>>;
	/** Every committed row of `q`, as `page`. */
	rows<C extends Columns, K extends readonly string[]>(table: Table<C, K>, q: Query<C, K>): AsyncIterable<RowOf<C>>;
	/** Writes `row` when the transaction commits (an upsert: the whole row replaced). */
	put<C extends Columns, K extends readonly string[]>(table: Table<C, K>, row: PutRowOf<C>): void;
	/** Changes the row with `key` when the transaction commits; an absent key changes nothing. */
	update<C extends Columns, K extends readonly string[]>(
		table: Table<C, K>,
		key: KeyOf<C, K>,
		set: SetOf<C, K> | ((row: ColumnRefs<C>) => SetOf<C, K>),
	): void;
	/** Deletes the row with `key` when the transaction commits. */
	delete<C extends Columns, K extends readonly string[]>(table: Table<C, K>, key: KeyOf<C, K>): void;
	/** Changes every row matching `where` when the transaction commits (one statement, its count recorded). */
	updateWhere<C extends Columns, K extends readonly string[]>(
		table: Table<C, K>,
		where: (row: ColumnRefs<C>) => Condition,
		set: SetOf<C, K> | ((row: ColumnRefs<C>) => SetOf<C, K>),
	): void;
	/** Deletes every row matching `where` when the transaction commits. */
	deleteWhere<C extends Columns, K extends readonly string[]>(
		table: Table<C, K>,
		where: (row: ColumnRefs<C>) => Condition,
	): void;
}

## ActivityCounts  chord/src/host/activity.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** What `host.activity` counts. */
export type ActivityCounts = {
	/** Holds arriving over links and served here. */
	readonly references: number;
	/** Method calls running on this host, local and remote. */
	readonly calls: number;
	/** Running jobs (slice 5). */
	readonly jobs: number;
	/** Objects kept live by their type's `linger` after their last reference. */
	readonly lingering: number;
};

## Admission  chord/src/host/admission.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** An admission's decision: the value the factory is handed about the caller, or a denial with the reason it is shown. */
export type Admission<T> =
	| { readonly kind: "allow"; readonly value: T }
	| { readonly kind: "deny"; readonly reason: string };

## Admit  chord/src/host/admission.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * A remote type's admission (`host.serve(Type, factory, { admit })`): synchronous and declarative, run first in every
 * attempt. Its attempt parks until what it declared is live and hydrated, then reads the decision and follows it: an
 * equal value changes nothing, another one rebuilds the object, a denial shows `failed { denied }`.
 */
export type Admit<C extends Contract, P extends Principal = Principal> = (
	params: ParamsOf<C>,
	principal: P,
	self: AdmitSelf,
) => Watchable<Admission<AdmittedOf<C>>>;

## AdmitSelf  chord/src/host/admission.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * What `admit` declares with, valid only while it runs: references (`at(key)` on their keyed members), registries,
 * derives and live queries. An admission decides and owns nothing: no documents, natives, routines or jobs.
 */
export type AdmitSelf = Pick<Self, "get" | "registry" | "derive" | "liveQuery">;

## allow  chord/src/host/admission.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * Allows the caller: `value` is what the factory is handed about it, plain JSON the contract's `admission` schema
 * describes (never validated). Small and rarely changing (a mode, a role): another value rebuilds the caller's object.
 */
export function allow<const T extends JsonValue>(value: T): Admission<T>

## deny  chord/src/host/admission.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** Denies the caller. `reason` reaches it as the message of its `forbidden` error: it is user-facing. */
export function deny(reason: string): Admission<never>

## BuiltQuery  chord/src/host/attempt.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** What a named query's builder returns: a query of the table (`C`, `K`), joined or not. */
export type BuiltQuery<C extends Columns, K extends readonly string[]> = {
	readonly table: TableDefinition<C, K>;
	readonly order: Order;
};

## Factory  chord/src/host/attempt.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * A factory: synchronous and declarative, run once per attempt. A remote one also gets the principal in its object's
 * identity and returns one variant, `{ variant, members }`; one of a contract that declares an `admission` gets the
 * admitted value after the principal (slice 14 §2.1: it selects the variant and the members, and `self.job` is
 * refused there). Methods get a `Ctx` for the app's principal type `P`.
 */
export type Factory<C extends Contract, P extends Principal = Principal> = ShapeOf<C>["kind"] extends "local"
	? (params: ParamsOf<C>, self: keyof ParamsOf<C> extends never ? StoreSelf<P> : Self<P>) => Implementation<C, Ctx<P>>
	: ShapeOf<C> extends { readonly admission: Schema }
		? (params: ParamsOf<C>, principal: P, admitted: AdmittedOf<C>, self: Self<P>) => Implementation<C, Ctx<P>>
		: (params: ParamsOf<C>, principal: P, self: Self<P>) => Implementation<C, Ctx<P>>;

## ListHandle  chord/src/host/attempt.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** What `self.list` returns: the list's value for a state member, and `more` for a method. */
export type ListHandle<T> = {
	/** The loaded rows in order, and whether rows may follow them. */
	readonly value: Watchable<{ rows: T[]; moreAfter: boolean }>;
	/** Loads one more page behind the last one; resolves once its rows are in `value`. */
	more(context: Context): Promise<null>;
};

## QueryBuilder  chord/src/host/attempt.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** A named query's builder: a pure function of the query's arguments. */
export type QueryBuilder<C extends Columns, K extends readonly string[], A> = (args: A) => BuiltQuery<C, K>;

## QueryBuilders  chord/src/host/attempt.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * The builders `self.queries` takes, by query name: a builder for a query the contract lists (the contract has its
 * argument schema), or `[argsSchema, builder]` for a query private to its owner.
 */
export type QueryBuilders<C extends Columns, K extends readonly string[], A> = {
	readonly [N in keyof A]: QueryBuilder<C, K, A[N]> | readonly [Schema, QueryBuilder<C, K, A[N]>];
};

## Self  chord/src/host/attempt.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * What a factory declares with. Declarations (`state`, `derive`, `get`, `registry`, `writable`, `events`, `retryOn`,
 * `open`, `on`, `onLive`, `job`; `table`, `query` and `contribute` in `StoreSelf`) are valid only while it runs. `P` is
 * the app's principal type, which the ctx of routine calls and job runs carry.
 */
export interface Self<P extends Principal = Principal> extends RoutineDeclarations<P> {
	/** This object's documents of `definition`, in memory for its life (across its attempts). */
	state<D extends StateDefinition<JsonObject, KeyedBy, false>>(definition: D): HandleOf<D>;
	/**
	 * A value computed from `sources` (JSON watchables and native ones: a `writable`, a registry value, `ref.state`) by
	 * the pure, synchronous `compute`; always JSON.
	 */
	derive<const S extends readonly (Watchable<unknown> | NativeWatchable<unknown>)[], T extends JsonValue>(
		sources: S,
		compute: (
			values: {
				readonly [I in keyof S]: S[I] extends Watchable<infer V>
					? V
					: S[I] extends NativeWatchable<infer V>
						? V
						: never;
			},
		) => T,
	): Watchable<T>;
	/** A reference to another object, live once this object is, released when it ends. */
	get<C extends Contract>(Type: C, params: ParamsOf<C>): Reference<C>;
	/**
	 * Registry `R`'s composed value as this plugin's version of `R` sees it: a declared dependency, as `get` is
	 * (the attempt parks until it has a usable value: `failed { waiting }` while it has none, woken when it has). Read
	 * `.value` at use; once live, a later failure of the registry keeps its last good value while every contribution it
	 * was built from is still in the table.
	 */
	registry<C, V>(R: Registry<C, V>): RegistryValue<V>;
	/**
	 * An in-process value this attempt sets (`set`, identity compared): a contribution, a derive source and an `on`
	 * source, never a state member; its watches end with the attempt, and `set` after its end throws `released`.
	 */
	writable<T>(initial: T): Writable<T>;
	/**
	 * An event source of this attempt (decision "Events: fire-and-forget members"), implementing an event member: `emit`
	 * delivers a JSON value once to each reference bound to the object before it, at the event flush (a microtask), after
	 * the state published before it; never kept, never folded, dropped for a holder that cannot keep up. Emits are no
	 * transaction work (`await self.tx(...)`, then `emit`); after the attempt's seal `emit` throws `released`.
	 */
	events<T>(): EventSource<T>;
	/**
	 * Wake signals: a new value of any of `sources` (registry values; constants never change) retries this object
	 * while it is failed, as `ref.retry()` does, and once more at once if its current activation fails. Followed from
	 * the factory's return until the next attempt's declaration or the object's end; failures wake nothing.
	 */
	retryOn(...sources: readonly (Watchable<unknown> | NativeWatchable<unknown>)[]): void;
	/**
	 * A native, opened during activation after the references are live and the earlier natives are open, and closed
	 * in reverse when the attempt ends. `open` gets a context aborted when the attempt is abandoned; `close` one aborted
	 * at the close timeout. Throw `broken(error)` from `open` when retrying is pointless.
	 */
	open<T>(
		open: (context: Context) => Promise<T>,
		close: (value: T, reason: NativeCloseReason, context: Context) => void | Promise<void>,
		options?: NativeOptions,
	): Native<T>;
	/** Runs `fn` as one transaction of this object (§9). */
	tx<R>(fn: (tx: Tx) => R | Promise<R>, context: Context): Promise<R>;
	/**
	 * A source following another runtime's synchronous observer (Durable's views, slice 6b §3): `attach` runs during
	 * activation once the natives opened (a rejection or `undefined` fails the activation `transient`), and the observer
	 * is detached when the attempt ends. Its runtime failing fails this object `transient`; its `ended` is final, the
	 * source keeping its last value. A state member, a derive source, an `on` source.
	 */
	follow<T>(attach: FollowAttach<T>): Watchable<T>;
	/**
	 * This object's job `definition` (§15), once per job name: `run` runs each started run outside transactions,
	 * `finish` records its outcome in one. Starts are taken once the object is live.
	 */
	job<A, R, S>(definition: JobDefinition<A, R, S>, implementation: JobImplementation<A, R, S, P>): JobHandle<A, R, S>;
	/**
	 * A named query read live (slice 14 §3): the first `range.first` rows of `query` for `args`, and whether a further
	 * row exists, as a JSON watchable. `args` may be a watchable of the arguments: the member shows the previous rows
	 * until the read for the new arguments has run. Opened once this object's dependencies are live; a commit that
	 * can change its rows runs it again in its step. Another object's query is read through its reference
	 * (`self.get(Store, {}).member.name`), the owner's own through what `self.queries` returned.
	 */
	liveQuery<T, A>(
		query: NamedQuery<T, A>,
		args: A | Watchable<A>,
		range: { readonly first: number },
	): Watchable<{ rows: T[]; more: boolean }>;
	/**
	 * The exact number of rows of a named query for `args`, live (slice 14 §3.1). Expensive, know what you are doing:
	 * every run reads every matching row, nothing caps it, and it runs again on every write to its tables except an
	 * `update` that assigns none of its condition's columns. Count what a key or an index bounds.
	 */
	count<T, A>(query: NamedQuery<T, A>, args: A | Watchable<A>): Watchable<number>;
	/**
	 * A list a screen loads more of (slice 14 §4): the rows of a named query in pages of `options.first` between
	 * fixed bookmarks, so loaded rows stay live, `more` sends only the new rows, and a row that moves leaves no gap
	 * and no duplicate. `name` is the list's within this object: its bookmarks survive a reload by it. One source,
	 * `[[namedQuery, args]]`; `args` may be a watchable of the arguments.
	 */
	list<T, A>(
		name: string,
		sources: readonly (readonly [NamedQuery<T, A>, A | Watchable<A>])[],
		options: ListOptions,
	): ListHandle<T>;
}

## StoreSelf  chord/src/host/attempt.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * What the factory of a `local` type with empty params declares with: one object per host and type, so its data may
 * persist (P3). `P` as for `Self`.
 */
export interface StoreSelf<P extends Principal = Principal> extends Self<P> {
	/** This object's documents of `definition`: in memory for its life, or persisted in the host's store. */
	state<D extends StateDefinition<JsonObject, KeyedBy, boolean>>(definition: D): HandleOf<D>;
	/** This object's table `definition` in the host's store, once per table name. */
	table<C extends Columns, K extends readonly string[]>(definition: TableDefinition<C, K>): Table<C, K>;
	/**
	 * A live query (decision "Live queries over an object's own tables"): the rows of `q` (at most `limit`, in its
	 * order) over `table`, a table this factory declared, as a JSON watchable (a state member, a derive source). Run
	 * before the object goes live, and again in the commit step of every commit of this object that writes `table`
	 * (one query per such commit, bounded by `limit`; not for tables written hundreds of times a second). A limit is
	 * required (`invalid/args`).
	 */
	query<C extends Columns, K extends readonly string[]>(
		table: Table<C, K>,
		q: Query<C, K>,
		limit: number,
	): Watchable<RowOf<C>[]>;
	/**
	 * Named queries over `table`, a table this factory declared (slice 14 §3.1): one per entry of `builders`, each a
	 * pure function of its arguments returning a query of the table. What it returns implements a `queries` member of
	 * the contract (the queries listed there; the others are private to this object and bring their argument schema).
	 * `options.map` turns a row (and a joined query's partner) into the item readers get, from the columns `reads`
	 * (and `partnerReads`) list: a change of another column is no change of the item.
	 */
	queries<C extends Columns, K extends readonly string[], T, A extends { readonly [query: string]: unknown }>(
		table: Table<C, K>,
		options: QueriesOptions<RowOf<C>, T>,
		builders: QueryBuilders<C, K, A>,
	): { readonly [N in keyof A]: NamedQuery<T, A[N]> };
	/**
	 * Contributes `value` to registry `R` from the moment this object is live until it ends, fails or restarts (R21: a
	 * host-lifetime object): a plain value, or a Chord watchable of one (followed: its change recomposes). At most one
	 * per registry.
	 */
	contribute<C>(R: Registry<C, unknown>, value: Contribution<C>): void;
}

## Ctx  chord/src/host/ctx.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** A handler's context. */
export interface Ctx<P extends Principal = Principal> extends Context {
	/** The caller as its link stamped it; on a local object's handler the host's principal (none on a client). */
	readonly principal: P | undefined;
	/** The calling host's incarnation over a link, this host's otherwise (R20). */
	readonly incarnation: string;
	/**
	 * A reference as the caller (`principal`) sees it, released when the handler settles; afterwards `get` throws
	 * `released`.
	 */
	get<C extends Contract>(Type: C, params: ParamsOf<C>, options?: GetOptions): Promise<Reference<C>>;
	/**
	 * Runs `fn` in a child span `name` of this ctx's span (`telemetry`) with its host's `chord.host` and `attributes`:
	 * `fn` gets a child ctx (the same principal, incarnation, signal and `get`, its references this ctx's), so calls
	 * inside are parented under it. A throw marks the span failed (`trace_failed`; a cancel keeps it ok) and is rethrown.
	 * Without an adapter that records, `fn` gets this ctx.
	 */
	trace<T>(name: string, attributes: SpanAttributes, fn: (ctx: Ctx<P>) => Promise<T>): Promise<T>;
}

## defineFacet  chord/src/host/facet.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** Defines a facet; base code binds `P` once, next to its principal type. */
export function defineFacet<P extends Principal>(setup: (host: FacetHost<P>, self: FacetSelf) => void): Facet<P>

## Facet  chord/src/host/facet.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** A plugin's facet for hosts of the app's principal type `P` (type only: nothing is checked at runtime). */
export type Facet<P extends Principal> = {
	readonly setup: (host: FacetHost<P>, self: FacetSelf) => void;
	/** Type only: the principal type, invariant, so a host takes only facets typed for exactly its `P`. */
	readonly "~principal"?: (principal: P) => P;
};

## FacetHost  chord/src/host/facet.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** What a setup serves types and registries with (valid only while the setup runs), and the host's presence lists. */
export interface FacetHost<P extends Principal = Principal> {
	/**
	 * Serves a type on this host with `factory`; a remote type's factory gets the principal its object is for.
	 * `options.accepts` maps the older versions it still serves (checked here: a declaration error rejects the load or
	 * the reload). A remote type whose contract declares an `admission` takes `options.admit` (required), and its
	 * factory the admitted value (slice 14 §2.1).
	 */
	serve<C extends Contract>(Type: C, factory: Factory<C, P>, ...options: ServeArguments<C, P>): void;
	/**
	 * Serves registry `R` on this host (its defining plugin's facet, the one provider, D1): `compose` builds the value
	 * from the table, `accepts` adapts older versions. A second serve of a registry is refused at `load`.
	 */
	serve<C, V>(R: Registry<C, V>, provider: RegistryProvider<C, V>): void;
	/** `host.references(Type)`: the references to objects of `Type` on this host (§19), for factories to derive from. */
	references<C extends Contract>(Type: C): Watchable<readonly Presence<C, P>[]>;
}

## FacetSelf  chord/src/host/facet.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** What a facet's setup declares with besides the host: its contributions to registries (R21). */
export interface FacetSelf {
	/**
	 * Contributes `value` to registry `R` while this plugin is loaded: a plain value, or a Chord watchable of one
	 * (followed: its change recomposes). At most one per registry.
	 */
	contribute<C>(R: Registry<C, unknown>, value: Contribution<C>): void;
}

## ServeArguments  chord/src/host/facet.ts
used by: chord-effect via FacetHost
/**
 * `host.serve`'s options argument: required, with `admit`, for a contract that declares an `admission`; optional
 * otherwise.
 */
export type ServeArguments<C extends Contract, P extends Principal = Principal> = ShapeOf<C> extends {
	readonly admission: Schema;
}
	? [options: ServeOptions<C, P> & { readonly admit: Admit<C, P> }]
	: [options?: ServeOptions<C, P>];

## ServeOptions  chord/src/host/facet.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** What `host.serve` takes besides the type and the factory. */
export type ServeOptions<C extends Contract = Contract, P extends Principal = Principal> = {
	/**
	 * The type's admission (slice 14 §2.1; remote types whose contract declares an `admission`, and only those: either
	 * without the other, or on a `local` type, is a declaration error): run first in every attempt, it reads data about
	 * the caller and returns a watchable of `allow(value)` or `deny(reason)`; the factory is handed the value.
	 */
	readonly admit?: Admit<C, P>;
	/**
	 * The older versions of `C` this provider still binds, with the mappings their edits need (Q10, `checkAccepts`):
	 * an older consumer's state members mapped per binding, its calls' arguments and results mapped.
	 */
	readonly accepts?: AcceptsTable<C>;
	/**
	 * How long, in milliseconds, a live object with params stays live after its last reference is released (0 by
	 * default): a reference within that time reuses it, with its documents and dependencies.
	 */
	readonly linger?: number;
	/**
	 * Its calls start no `chord.method` span (`true`): Chord's telemetry ingest, whose every call would otherwise record
	 * a span about the telemetry it writes. Traced by default.
	 */
	readonly untraced?: true;
};

## FollowAttach  chord/src/host/follow.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * What `self.follow` takes: attaches `observer`, resolving with the attachment, `undefined` for an absent address.
 * The observer takes calls of any value (it only records them), so `T` is inferred from the attachment alone.
 */
export type FollowAttach<T> = (
	observer: FollowObserver<unknown>,
	context: Context,
) => Promise<FollowAttachment<T> | undefined>;

## FollowAttachment  chord/src/host/follow.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** What attaching gives: the value every later call starts from, and how to detach (Durable's `Observation`). */
export type FollowAttachment<T> = { readonly value: T; detach(): void };

## FollowObserver  chord/src/host/follow.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** The observer a followed runtime is given: Chord's watch shapes (Durable's `Observer`). */
export type FollowObserver<T> = {
	/** One change, synchronously and quickly: Chord only records it. */
	advance(call: WatchCall<T>, context: Context): void;
	/** The followed source ended: `failed` (its runtime failed), or `ended` for good. */
	end(end: WatchEnd): void;
};

## CommittedReload  chord/src/host/host.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * What a reload's commit applied, by plugin name: the `details.committed` of the `aborted` error of a reload whose
 * context aborted after its commit (the commit stands; only the wait for the report ended).
 */
export type CommittedReload = {
	readonly added: readonly string[];
	readonly changed: readonly string[];
	readonly removed: readonly string[];
	/** The plugins whose new code failed: they kept their old code (an added one was left out). */
	readonly failed: readonly string[];
};

## Host  chord/src/host/host.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** A host. `P` is the app's principal type, `R` its revocation type. */
export interface Host<P extends Principal = Principal, R extends JsonValue = JsonValue> {
	/** This host's address (`HostOptions.address`); `undefined` on a client. */
	readonly address: Address | undefined;
	/** This run of the host, sent in every handshake (R20): a link's peer sees it as its calls' `ctx.incarnation`. */
	readonly incarnation: string;
	/**
	 * The attributes this host's spans record for `principal`: its `principalAttributes` hook's, else `chord.principal`,
	 * its principal key; none without a principal.
	 */
	principalAttributes(principal: P | undefined, context: Context): Readonly<SpanAttributes>;
	/**
	 * Runs every facet's setup and publishes what they declared in one batch (the types and registries served, the
	 * registries composed once, the contributions); holds that waited for the publication are placed after that batch,
	 * and a registry with contributions and no provider is reported (`registry_undeclared`). Then activates every
	 * served type with empty params and resolves when each has had its first outcome (the start barrier, decision (a)):
	 * live, failed by its own cause, parked with no blocker here still without its first outcome, or ended (failures go
	 * to `onError`). A plugin whose setup throws or is refused at declaration (a name given twice, a type or registry
	 * another plugin serves, a remote type here without principal or address, `checkAccepts`) is left out and reported
	 * (`failed`); it never closes the host. A name that is no npm name throws before anything changes. Runs once.
	 */
	load(facets: readonly PluginFacet<P>[], context: Context): Promise<LoadReport>;
	/**
	 * Reloads this host's plugins (slice 7b): `facets` is its complete new plugin set; a plugin in it and not loaded
	 * is added, one loaded with another facet value is changed (the same facet object is unchanged: untouched), one
	 * loaded and not in it is removed. Staging runs every new setup and every affected object's new factory against a
	 * recording `self`, per plugin: a plugin whose new code fails there keeps its old code (an added one is left out),
	 * and so does a changed plugin whose recorded requests would not bind because of it (the closure rule); both are
	 * reported (`failed`); `options.failed` names plugins the caller passes as their loaded facet because their new
	 * code failed before (a build, an evaluation): the same for the closure rule and the report. Then it commits in one
	 * batch (types, registries, contributions; a publication waking the requests for the names it serves) and every
	 * object of a changed or removed plugin takes its fate: restarted (its old attempt finishing old work first),
	 * retried, or ended (its type removed). Resolves with the report once every fate started (retries checked their
	 * dependencies; a restart reports what its readiness found at once; it does not wait for objects to go live).
	 * Reloads run one after another. Throws before `load` resolved and for a name that is no npm name (before anything
	 * changes); rejects `released/closed` after `close`; `context`'s abort before the commit rejects `aborted` and
	 * changes nothing, after it only ends the wait (`aborted`, its `details.committed` naming what the commit applied:
	 * `CommittedReload`).
	 */
	reload(facets: readonly PluginFacet<P>[], context: Context, options?: ReloadOptions): Promise<ReloadReport>;
	/**
	 * A reference once its object is live (and hydrated). It acts as the host's principal and goes where its type's host
	 * address puts it: here, over a route, or over the parent link (`Destination`). It waits while the reference is
	 * `loading`, `failed { transient }` or `failed { waiting }` until its `readyTimeout`, then rejects with the last
	 * cause and releases the reference; a broken failure rejects at once, and so does a get before `load` (`not_ready`).
	 */
	get<C extends Contract>(Type: C, params: ParamsOf<C>, context: Context, options?: GetOptions): Promise<Reference<C>>;
	/**
	 * A reference at once, following its object until released: loading, live, failed (retried as its object is) and
	 * loading again while its link is down; it never rejects. Throws at once only for invalid params and before `load`
	 * (`not_ready`). A type not served where it goes is `failed { waiting }` (bound when a publication serves it;
	 * reported `unbound_long` after 5 s); a `hostAddress` or route that refuses fails it broken. Its `variant` is
	 * `undefined` until its first binding.
	 */
	hold<C extends Contract>(Type: C, params: ParamsOf<C>, context: Context, options?: GetOptions): Held<C>;
	/**
	 * A link from a child: this host serves its remote types over it, every hold and call arriving on it acting as
	 * `principal`. `context` is the parent of the work arriving on it (its cancellation is dropped).
	 */
	accept(link: Link, options: LinkOptions<P>, context: Context): void;
	/**
	 * This host's parent link: remote types not served here and not routed are held over it, every such reference held
	 * again on a new one; holds arriving on it may name whom they act for. Throws while the previous one is open; once
	 * it closed (a drop), `connect` takes the next. `principal` is who the parent is.
	 */
	connect(link: Link, options: LinkOptions<P>, context: Context): void;
	/**
	 * How this host reaches hosts of `Kind` (called before `load`, once per kind): `authorize` admits every hold routed
	 * over it, `resolve` makes the link of an address, for a new hold, on `retry`, or once after a link that completed
	 * its handshake dropped while held (no timer). A rejected `resolve`, or a link closed before its handshake, fails the
	 * address's holders `failed { waiting }` (they stay on its path). With `admit` (slice 14 §2.3) nothing is resolved
	 * or forwarded for a principal before the route's decision allows it. `context` is the parent of the route's work
	 * (its `resolve`s, the holds and calls on its links, its admission's references), aborted for it when this host
	 * closes. Returns the address controls.
	 */
	route<N extends string, Q extends Params>(
		Kind: HostKind<N, Q>,
		options: RouteOptions<P, HostKind<N, Q>>,
		context: Context,
	): RouteHandle<HostKind<N, Q>>;
	/**
	 * Revokes `revocation` (§4, R10, R11), synchronously: every remote object whose principal it revokes (`revokedBy`)
	 * ends at once, whatever references remain (holders get `forbidden`, running calls are aborted, an activation is
	 * abandoned); every child link whose principal it revokes closes (never the parent, never this host's own
	 * principal); and every route link is sent `revoke`, which the host there applies with its own `revokedBy`. Nothing
	 * is replayed to links made later.
	 */
	revoke(revocation: R, context: Context): void;
	/**
	 * The references to objects of `Type` on this host (§19), one entry per reference: the object's params, the
	 * principal it acts as (remote types) and its origin, the incarnation of the host it was made for (two tabs are two
	 * origins). Changes in the batch where a reference binds or ends; a link drop is a departure.
	 */
	references<C extends Contract>(Type: C): Watchable<readonly Presence<C, P>[]>;
	/**
	 * The work keeping this host busy, for the app's supervisor: holds arriving over links and served here, method
	 * calls running, running jobs and lingering objects; published at most once per microtask turn with changes.
	 */
	readonly activity: Watchable<ActivityCounts>;
	/**
	 * Registry `R`'s composed value as `R`'s version sees it, for code outside objects, once it is usable: waits while it
	 * has no value (`unavailable/undeclared` without a provider, a first `compose` that threw, a version not served
	 * here: `contract_mismatch`) until its `readyTimeout`, then rejects with the last error; before `load` it rejects
	 * `not_ready` at once.
	 */
	registry<C, V>(R: Registry<C, V>, context: Context, options?: GetOptions): Promise<RegistryValue<V>>;
	/**
	 * Runs `fn` with a call context for code outside objects (a Durable tool, a CLI): the host's principal (or
	 * `options.principal`; an explicit `undefined` runs anonymous), this host's incarnation, `context`'s telemetry and signal, `ctx.get`. When `fn` settles or
	 * `context` aborts, the context is sealed: its signal aborted, `ctx.get` refused `released`, every reference it took
	 * released; an abort rejects at once. `host.close` seals the open ones; after it, `root` rejects `released`.
	 */
	root<T>(fn: (ctx: Ctx<P>) => Promise<T>, context: Context, options?: RootOptions<P>): Promise<T>;
	/**
	 * The records and rows of this host's store belonging to `address` (host-keyed documents, `host(...)` cells) as a
	 * store archive with `host` in its manifest, holding the store's commit queue while it is read. Throws
	 * `invalid/args` without a store.
	 */
	exportHostData(address: Address, context: Context): AsyncIterableIterator<ArchivePart>;
	/**
	 * Imports a host's data archive (`exportHostData`'s) into this host's store in one commit,
	 * under `options.address` (a copy) or the archive's; data of that address refused, or replaced with `existing:
	 * "replace"`; older tables' rows migrated through their owners' histories. One operation at a time; activations
	 * wait while one runs; the live owners' lines are held and what they hold of the address is adopted in one batch
	 * (spec `docs/host-keyed/spec.md` §5). Rejects `invalid/args` without a store, for a refused archive or existing
	 * data; `released` once `context` aborted before the commit was admitted.
	 */
	importHostData(
		parts: AsyncIterable<unknown> | Iterable<unknown>,
		context: Context,
		options?: HostImportOptions,
	): Promise<HostDataCounts>;
	/**
	 * Deletes the records and rows belonging to `address` in one commit, coordinated as `importHostData`. With
	 * `options.plugin` (slice 14 §6), only what that plugin's objects own: the documents and tables of the types it
	 * serves here now (a session moving to another app drops the old app's data of it). Data under a type the plugin
	 * served before and serves no more (a renamed type) is not its any more and stays; a plugin not loaded here is
	 * `invalid/args`.
	 */
	deleteHostData(address: Address, context: Context, options?: HostDeleteOptions): Promise<HostDataCounts>;
	/**
	 * Closes its links, seals its root scopes, then ends every object at once, then drains and closes them one by one,
	 * the last to go live first (reason `close`). Rejects with an `AggregateError` of the closes that threw.
	 */
	close(context: Context): Promise<void>;
}

## HostDeleteOptions  chord/src/host/host.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** What `host.deleteHostData` takes besides the address: the one plugin whose data of it is deleted. */
export type HostDeleteOptions = { readonly plugin?: string };

## HostError  chord/src/host/host.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * What `onError` gets, by kind. `object` is the object's type, with its params key when it has params; `failure` is a
 * `FailureCause`, `error` the plain error.
 */
export type HostError =
	| BatchError
	| RegistryError
	| UnboundLong
	| TransactionCancelled
	| { readonly kind: "activation_failed"; readonly object: string; readonly failure: FailureCause }
	/** A live object failed at runtime (a `migrate` failing on access, a stored version newer than the code). */
	| { readonly kind: "object_failed"; readonly object: string; readonly failure: FailureCause }
	/** The host's store stopped after a backend error: the host closes itself (once). */
	| { readonly kind: "storage_failed"; readonly error: unknown }
	| { readonly kind: "close_failed"; readonly object: string; readonly native: Position; readonly error: unknown }
	| { readonly kind: "close_timeout"; readonly object: string; readonly native: Position }
	| { readonly kind: "drain_timeout"; readonly object: string }
	/**
	 * An event mapping for an older consumer threw (decision "Events: fire-and-forget members"): that emit is dropped for
	 * that version only; once per failure episode (the next mapped emit ends it).
	 */
	| {
			readonly kind: "event_mapping_failed";
			readonly object: string;
			readonly member: string;
			readonly version: number;
			readonly error: unknown;
	  }
	| { readonly kind: "protocol_error"; readonly error: unknown }
	| { readonly kind: "resolve_failed"; readonly address: string; readonly error: unknown }
	/**
	 * A derive's compute threw (its owner's, once per failure episode: the first failure after a value or after its
	 * creation; a value ends the episode); `member` when it is an exposed state member.
	 */
	| { readonly kind: "derive_failed"; readonly object: string; readonly member?: string; readonly error: unknown }
	/**
	 * A live read's run failed after its object went live (a row its code cannot read, a set nobody serves), once per
	 * failure episode (a good run ends it): the member is failed until then. `query` is the table's name for
	 * `self.query`, the named query's label for `self.liveQuery`, `self.count` and `self.list`.
	 */
	| { readonly kind: "query_failed"; readonly object: string; readonly query: string; readonly error: unknown }
	/** A routine's call threw, or its source failed for good; `routine` is its kind and position. */
	| { readonly kind: "routine_failed"; readonly object: string; readonly routine: Position; readonly error: unknown }
	/** A job's `run` threw (not after an abort): its outcome is `failed { threw }`. */
	| {
			readonly kind: "job_failed";
			readonly object: string;
			readonly job: string;
			readonly id: string;
			readonly error: unknown;
	  }
	/** A job's `finish` threw: retried with backoff, blocked after five failures in a row. */
	| {
			readonly kind: "job_finish_failed";
			readonly object: string;
			readonly job: string;
			readonly id: string;
			readonly error: unknown;
	  }
	/** A persisted run was cut off five times in a row by crashes (D6): it ends `failed { restart_limit }`, `finish` runs. */
	| {
			readonly kind: "job_interrupted";
			readonly object: string;
			readonly job: string;
			readonly id: string;
			readonly restarts: number;
	  }
	/** A blocked run was dropped without `finish`: aborted, or its object ended. */
	| { readonly kind: "job_dropped"; readonly object: string; readonly job: string; readonly id: string }
	/**
	 * An attempt parked longer than `readyTimeout` (since `since`, `Date.now()` time), whatever its blocker: once per
	 * parking episode, naming the first blocker in declaration order (`waitingFor`, a reference's label or `registry
	 * <name>`) and its `state`; a diagnostic of a ring across hosts started at the same moment or a long wait (nothing
	 * fails).
	 */
	| {
			readonly kind: "parked_long";
			readonly object: string;
			readonly waitingFor: string;
			readonly state: "loading" | "failed";
			readonly since: number;
	  };

## HostOptions  chord/src/host/host.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** What `createHost` takes; `R` is the app's revocation type (JSON). */
export type HostOptions<P extends Principal = Principal, R extends JsonValue = JsonValue> = {
	/** This host's address (`Session({ id })`): it serves only objects placed there. Without one, a client. */
	readonly address?: Address;
	/** Who this host acts as for its own requests; a host without one (a client) has none. */
	readonly principal?: P;
	/** The key of a principal in identities; L1's canonical JSON by default. The same function on every host. */
	readonly principalKey?: PrincipalKeyFunction<P>;
	/**
	 * The telemetry adapter (§29): this host's root spans (activations, closes, resolves, routines, methods called over
	 * links) and metrics, and the carriers its links extract; NOOP by default, which records nothing and costs one call
	 * per span site.
	 */
	readonly telemetry?: TelemetryContext;
	/**
	 * Who a span was for (decision "Who a span was for"): the attributes its method and call spans record for a
	 * principal, in place of the default `chord.principal` (its principal key, capped at 256 characters). Called for
	 * every span recorded with a principal: synchronous and cheap; caching, if any, is the hook's own. The same
	 * function on every host.
	 */
	readonly principalAttributes?: PrincipalAttributes<P>;
	/** Everything that fails in the background; every app handles it. */
	readonly onError: (error: HostError) => void;
	/** How long a native's close, and an ending object's running calls, are waited for; 30 s by default. */
	readonly closeTimeout?: number;
	/** How long an activation attempt, and a `get`, may take until the object is live; 60 s by default. */
	readonly readyTimeout?: number;
	/**
	 * How long a reload's restart keeps its old attempt open for old work (its calls, routed calls, its successor's
	 * readiness) before it is sealed and anything still running is cut off (`released`); 5 s by default, at most
	 * `closeTimeout`. Ends in seconds the waits Chord cannot see (a root opened without the method's `ctx`).
	 */
	readonly reloadDrainTimeout?: number;
	/**
	 * The heartbeat of every link: a link silent for `ping` ms (15 s by default) sends a `ping`; one silent for `close`
	 * ms (30 s by default), its handshake included, is closed.
	 */
	readonly heartbeat?: { readonly ping?: number; readonly close?: number };
	/**
	 * How many concurrent calls of one origin this host accepts on a link it was not given as trusted (its call window,
	 * announced in `hello`); 10,000 by default, a positive integer. On a trusted link it announces none (decision "Call
	 * windows only for untrusted links"): the app's own hosts never queue calls behind each other.
	 */
	readonly callWindow?: number;
	/**
	 * How many `event` messages of its own this host leaves unacknowledged per link and origin (decision "Events:
	 * fire-and-forget members"); 32 by default. A flush finding the window full drops that origin's events (counted):
	 * nothing waits for a slow consumer.
	 */
	readonly eventWindow?: number;
	/**
	 * What revokes a principal (§4): `host.revoke(r)` ends the objects and closes the child links of every principal
	 * `p` whose `revokedBy(p)` holds `r` (compared as canonical JSON). The same function on every host.
	 */
	readonly revokedBy?: RevokedBy<P, R>;
	/**
	 * A synchronous compressor (`nodeCompression` for Node): JSON parts above 16 KiB this host originates are deflated
	 * once, and deflated parts it owns inflated in place. Without one (a browser), nothing is compressed and deflated
	 * parts are inflated asynchronously, later messages of their link waiting in order.
	 */
	readonly compression?: Compression;
	/**
	 * The store persisted documents and tables live in (`openStore`); the app owns it and closes it after the host.
	 * One open host per store. A `storage_failed` of the store is reported once and closes the host.
	 */
	readonly store?: Store;
};

## LinkOptions  chord/src/host/host.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * What `accept` and `connect` take: the principal of the host at the other end, as this host stamps it; `trusted` skips
 * the message check on the link (IPC to the host's own processes; never grants the principal fields); the codec both
 * ends of the link use (`binaryCodec` by default); and the limits per part of what arrives on it (Q2: none on a
 * trusted link, 16 MiB on the wire and 64 MiB decoded otherwise, unless set).
 */
export type LinkOptions<P extends Principal = Principal> = {
	readonly principal: P;
	readonly trusted?: boolean;
	readonly codec?: Codec;
	readonly limits?: PartLimits;
};

## ReloadedObject  chord/src/host/host.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * One object's fate in a reload: `restarted` (its old attempt drained, sealed and closed with reason `reload`, a new
 * attempt on the new code), `ended` (its type is gone), `parked` (its new code waits for a failed dependency,
 * `cause`), or `retried` (it was failed, parked or activating: a new attempt runs on the new code).
 */
export type ReloadedObject = { readonly object: string } & (
	| { readonly kind: "restarted" }
	| { readonly kind: "ended" }
	| { readonly kind: "parked"; readonly cause: FailureCause }
	| { readonly kind: "retried" }
);

## ReloadReport  chord/src/host/host.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * What a reload did (slice 7b §1): its plugins by change (those applied), the plugins whose new code failed, and what
 * every affected object did.
 */
export type ReloadReport = {
	readonly plugins: {
		readonly added: readonly string[];
		readonly changed: readonly string[];
		readonly removed: readonly string[];
	};
	readonly failed: readonly PluginFailure[];
	/** Every live, activating, parked or failed object of a changed or removed plugin, by its label. */
	readonly objects: readonly ReloadedObject[];
};

## Presence  chord/src/host/presence.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * One reference to an object of `C`: the object's params, the principal it acts as (for a remote type), and its
 * incarnation: the host that made it as its caller sees it (a hold's caller over a link; two tabs are two
 * incarnations), the word `ctx.incarnation` uses.

	readonly incarnation: string;

## RefState  chord/src/host/ref-state.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * Where a reference stands. `loading`: its object activates, retries or is parked on dependencies still under way, it
 * waits for its host's publication or a parent link, or its link is down (the reference's coarser view of its object's
 * waiting and activating); `failed`: its object failed and no attempt runs (`transient`: `retryAt` is when its backoff
 * retries it; `broken`: no automatic retry), or nothing fits it or its object is parked on a failed dependency
 * (`waiting`: an event wakes it, `retryAt` undefined); `live`: bound; `ended`: for good, with the error that says why
 * (`released` without a reason: released by its holder; `released/ended`: its object ended; `released/closed`: its
 * host closed; `forbidden/revoked`).
 */
export type RefState =
	| { readonly kind: "loading" }
	| { readonly kind: "live" }
	| { readonly kind: "failed"; readonly cause: FailureCause; readonly retryAt: number | undefined }
	| { readonly kind: "ended"; readonly error: ChordError };

## Held  chord/src/host/reference.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** What `host.hold` returns: a reference whose `variant` is `undefined` until its first binding. */
export type Held<C extends Contract> = ShapeOf<C>["kind"] extends "local"
	? Implementation<C> & Lifecycle
	: InVariants<C, undefined>;

## InVariants  chord/src/host/reference.ts
used by: chord-effect via Held
/** One member of a remote reference's union per variant; `Unbound` is what `variant` may also be. */
type InVariants<C extends Contract, Unbound> = {
	[V in keyof CurrentVariants<C>]: { readonly variant: V | Unbound } & VariantImplementation<CurrentVariants<C>[V]> &
		Lifecycle;
}[keyof CurrentVariants<C>];

## Lifecycle  chord/src/host/reference.ts
used by: chord-effect via Held
/** What every reference has besides its members. */
type Lifecycle = {
	/** The reference's state: loading, live, failed or released; watches get every change. */
	readonly state: NativeWatchable<RefState>;
	/**
	 * Asks a failed object for an attempt now (the backoff skipped, a broken one renewed); an object parked on failed
	 * dependencies passes it on to them, once; otherwise nothing.
	 */
	retry(): void;
	release(): void;
};

## Reference  chord/src/host/reference.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * A reference: a local contract's members, or for a remote contract the members of the variant its object chose,
 * narrowed by `variant`; and its state, `retry()` and `release()`. Every use after release throws.
 */
export type Reference<C extends Contract> = ShapeOf<C>["kind"] extends "local"
	? Implementation<C> & Lifecycle
	: InVariants<C, never>;

## RefIn  chord/src/host/reference.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** A remote reference narrowed to some of its variants. */
export type RefIn<C extends Contract, V extends string> = Extract<Reference<C>, { readonly variant: V }>;

## RevokedBy  chord/src/host/revocation.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** What revokes a principal: the app's typed values, the same function on every host. */
export type RevokedBy<P extends Principal, R extends JsonValue> = (principal: P) => readonly R[];

## RootOptions  chord/src/host/root.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** What `host.root` takes besides `fn` and the context. */
export type RootOptions<P extends Principal = Principal> = {
	/**
	 * Whom the scope acts as: the host's principal when omitted; a trusted same-host caller's choice (base code), an
	 * explicit `undefined` anonymous (`ctx.principal` undefined).
	 */
	readonly principal?: P | undefined;
	/**
	 * Runs `fn` in a new root span of this host's adapter (a click, a command: a trace of its own), `ctx.telemetry` that
	 * span, with its host's `chord.host` and `attributes`; a throw marks it failed (`trace_failed`, a cancel keeps it
	 * ok). Without an adapter that records, nothing is started.
	 */
	readonly trace?: { readonly name: string; readonly attributes?: SpanAttributes };
};

## RouteHandle  chord/src/host/route.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** What `host.route` returns: the app's controls of its addresses (D10b, R1). */
export type RouteHandle<K extends KindShape> = {
	/**
	 * Resolves `address` again now if it has holders and no link: its failure and its suspension end (a Retry button);
	 * an address nobody holds resolves at its next hold, and so does one whose holds the route's admission all denies
	 * or has not decided yet (nothing starts for them).
	 */
	retry(address: Address<K>): void;
	/**
	 * Resolves nothing for `address` while it has holders: they wait `failed { waiting }` ("suspended") once its link is
	 * gone; the suspension ends with its last holder or `retry`.
	 */
	suspend(address: Address<K>): void;
};

## RouteOptions  chord/src/host/route.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** What `host.route` takes for a kind. */
export type RouteOptions<P extends Principal, K extends KindShape> = {
	/** Whether `principal` may reach `address`; runs for every hold routed over the route, before anything starts. */
	authorize(principal: P, address: Address<K>): boolean;
	/**
	 * The link to `address`: `principal` is who the host at the other end is, `trusted` skips the message check on it,
	 * `limits` bound its parts (as `accept`'s). `context` is the route's, aborted when this host closes. Runs at most
	 * once at a time per address. `opened` is called once, when the link's handshake completed, with the incarnation of
	 * the host at the other end (its calls' `ctx.incarnation`): before anything else that host sent is handled and
	 * before this host sends on the link, so whoever resolves knows which run of the host its link reaches before that
	 * host's first call runs; never for a link that closes before its handshake. It must not throw.
	 */
	resolve(
		address: Address<K>,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<{
		readonly link: Link;
		readonly principal: P;
		readonly trusted?: boolean;
		readonly codec?: Codec;
		readonly limits?: PartLimits;
		readonly opened?: (incarnation: string) => void;
	}>;
	/**
	 * The route's admission (slice 14 §2.3): asked once per principal and address with holds on the route, after
	 * `authorize`, before anything is resolved or forwarded for that principal. It declares what it reads (references,
	 * registries, derives, live queries, acting as this host) and returns a watchable of `allow(null)` or
	 * `deny(reason)`: until its first allow a hold is `loading`; a denial fails the principal's holds to the address
	 * `failed { denied }`, releases them at the address's host and rejects their calls `forbidden/revoked`; a later allow
	 * shows them `loading` and forwards them again. While what it reads has failed, the holds bound on the address's
	 * link stay, new ones wait, and a new link of the address holds nothing until it can be read again (fail closed).
	 * **It reads only contracts the app's API owns**: a route is base
	 * code, it never reloads and keeps the contract tokens it was built with. It may hold nothing placed behind this
	 * route (`invalid/cycle`). **With `admit`, `resolve` must return the link to the final provider that serves the
	 * address**, never to another relay: a hold released by a denial is forwarded again under its id once a `ping`
	 * sent on the allow was answered, which proves the released hold's replies have all arrived only when the peer
	 * that answers is the one that sent them.
	 */
	admit?(principal: P, address: Address<K>, self: AdmitSelf): Watchable<Admission<null>>;
};

## NativeWatchValueCall  chord/src/host/routines.ts

/** A native watch's value call. */
export type NativeWatchValueCall<T> = Extract<NativeWatchCall<T>, { readonly kind: "value" }>;

## OnHandler  chord/src/host/routines.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * A routine's handler of a JSON source: the value call (the value, the ops since the previous call, whether the
 * source's document was retired since then) and the call's ctx. Failures are not calls of a handler (design §11): the
 * routine waits for the next value.
 */
export type OnHandler<T, C extends Ctx = Ctx> = (call: WatchValueCall<T>, ctx: C) => void | Promise<void>;

## OnLiveHandler  chord/src/host/routines.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** An `onLive` routine: called once its owner is live. */
export type OnLiveHandler<C extends Ctx = Ctx> = (ctx: C) => void | Promise<void>;

## OnNativeHandler  chord/src/host/routines.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** A routine's handler of a native source: the value call (the value) and the call's ctx. */
export type OnNativeHandler<T, C extends Ctx = Ctx> = (call: NativeWatchValueCall<T>, ctx: C) => void | Promise<void>;

## RoutineDeclarations  chord/src/host/routines.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** What the declarations of an owner (`on`, `onLive`) take; part of the factory's `self` and the facet's. */
export interface RoutineDeclarations<P extends Principal = Principal> {
	/**
	 * A routine over `source`: `fn` gets its current value first (ops `[["r", value]]`), then one call per change,
	 * never overlapping: changes during a call fold into one next call (the newest value, the ops since the previous
	 * call, `retired` when any of them was a retirement). After a call that threw, it is called again with the whole
	 * newest value (`retired` again if the call that threw had it) after a backoff (1 s doubling to 60 s), or at once on
	 * a change during the backoff. Ends with its source. A JSON watchable is one whose watch is Chord's shared `Watch`
	 * (every Chord and Durable source).
	 */
	on<T>(source: Watchable<T>, fn: OnHandler<T, Ctx<P>>): void;
	/**
	 * A routine over a native source (a registry value, `ref.state`): one whose watch is Chord's shared `NativeWatch`.
	 * As above without ops: after a busy call, one call with the newest value.
	 */
	on<T>(source: NativeWatchable<T>, fn: OnNativeHandler<T, Ctx<P>>): void;
	/**
	 * A routine called once its owner is live. Returning ends it; a throw is reported and restarts it after a backoff
	 * (1 s doubling to 60 s, reset after a run of a minute); the owner's end aborts its ctx.
	 */
	onLive(fn: OnLiveHandler<Ctx<P>>): void;
}

export type WatchValueCall<T> = Extract<WatchCall<T>, { readonly kind: "value" }>;

## defineJob  chord/src/jobs/definition.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** Declares a job: owned work a call starts that outlives it (§15). */
export function defineJob<
	const A extends Schema,
	const R extends Schema,
	D extends StateDefinition<JsonObject, false, boolean> | undefined = undefined,
>(name: string, options: JobOptions<A, R, D>): JobDefinition<Static<A>, Static<R>, StateOf<D>>

## JobAccepts  chord/src/jobs/definition.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** Per older version, its mappings forwards: its args to the current args, its result to the current result. */
export type JobAccepts<A extends Schema = Schema, R extends Schema = Schema> = {
	readonly [version: number]: { readonly args: (old: never) => Static<A>; readonly result: (old: never) => Static<R> };
};

## JobDefinition  chord/src/jobs/definition.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** A declared job; `A`, `R` and `S` are its args, result and state document (`undefined` without one). */
export class JobDefinition<A, R, S> {
	readonly name: string
	readonly version: number
	/** The args schema, Chord's copy; its compiled check is cached by this snapshot. */
	readonly args: Snapshot
	readonly result: Snapshot
	readonly state: StateDefinition<JsonObject, false, boolean> | undefined
	readonly concurrency: number | undefined
	/** The older versions' mappings, checked at declaration; slice 7 maps older runs with them. */
	readonly accepts: JobAccepts
	/** How its runs persist; `undefined` for a job in memory. */
	readonly persist: JobPersistence | undefined
	/** `hash64` of its args', result's and state's normal forms: a stored run of another fingerprint is blocked. */
	readonly fingerprint: string
	/** Type only: the args, result and state types. */
	declare readonly "~types"?: { readonly args: A; readonly result: R; readonly state: S }
	constructor(
		name: string,
		version: number,
		args: Snapshot,
		result: Snapshot,
		state: StateDefinition<JsonObject, false, boolean> | undefined,
		concurrency: number | undefined,
		accepts: JobAccepts,
		persist: JobPersistence | undefined,
		fingerprint: string,
	)
}

## JobError  chord/src/jobs/definition.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * Why a run failed: `run` threw (reported as `job_failed`; anything but a ChordError or PluginError becomes a
 * PluginError `internal` with its message), it was aborted (`abort`: `abort(id)`; `restart`: cut off by its attempt's
 * seal while the object continues, or a persisted run abandoned after a crash; `reload` comes with slice 7), or a
 * persisted run was cut off five times in a row (`restart_limit`, D6).
 */
export type JobError =
	| { readonly kind: "threw"; readonly error: ChordError | PluginError }
	| { readonly kind: "aborted"; readonly reason: "abort" | "reload" | "restart" }
	| { readonly kind: "restart_limit"; readonly restarts: number };

## JobOptions  chord/src/jobs/definition.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** What `defineJob` takes besides the name. */
export type JobOptions<
	A extends Schema,
	R extends Schema,
	D extends StateDefinition<JsonObject, false, boolean> | undefined,
> = {
	/** The job's version; every change of its args, result or state bumps it. */
	readonly version: number;
	/** The run's arguments: closed objects, JSON only (`running` carries them), checked at every start. */
	readonly args: A;
	/** What `run` returns; not validated. */
	readonly result: R;
	/**
	 * A singleton document definition: one document per run, `ctx.state` in `run`, `outcome.state` in `finish`; a
	 * persisted job's is persisted (`persist: true`, its `checkpointWhen`).
	 */
	readonly state?: D;
	/** At most this many runs running or finishing per object; a start beyond it rejects `unavailable/busy`. */
	readonly concurrency?: number;
	/** Per older version, how its args and result map forwards (used from slice 7 on; checked now). */
	readonly accepts?: JobAccepts<A, R>;
	/**
	 * Persists the runs in the object's store (slice 6b; only in `local` types with empty params, P3): how a run cut
	 * off by a crash or a stop resumes, `rerun` (its `run` again: idempotent work) or `abandon` (`finish` gets `failed {
	 * aborted, reason: "restart" }`). Its result is JSON only (no `bytes()`).
	 */
	readonly persist?: JobPersistence;
};

## JobPersistence  chord/src/jobs/definition.ts
used by: chord-effect via JobDefinition
/** How a persisted job's runs resume after a crash or a stop. */
export type JobPersistence = { readonly resume: "rerun" | "abandon" };

## Outcome  chord/src/jobs/definition.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** What a run ended with, as `finish` and `outcome` get it: its args and state, and its result or its error. */
export type Outcome<A, R, S> = { readonly id: string; readonly args: A; readonly state: S } & (
	| { readonly kind: "done"; readonly result: R }
	| { readonly kind: "failed"; readonly error: JobError }
);

## StateOf  chord/src/jobs/definition.ts
used by: chord-effect via defineJob
/** The value of a job's state document: the definition's document, `undefined` without one. */
type StateOf<D> = D extends StateDefinition<infer T, false, boolean> ? T : undefined;

## JobCtx  chord/src/jobs/job.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** A run's ctx: a handler's ctx (the object's principal or the host's), its run's id and, with a state, the state. */
export type JobCtx<P extends Principal, S> = Ctx<P> & { readonly jobId: string } & ([S] extends [undefined]
		? unknown
		: { readonly state: RunState<S> });

## JobHandle  chord/src/jobs/job.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** A job's handle, `self.job(Job, { run, finish? })`; `A`, `R` and `S` are its args, result and state. */
export interface JobHandle<A, R, S> {
	/**
	 * Starts a run in one transaction on the object's line and resolves with its `Run` after the commit: the args
	 * checked (`invalid/args`); a `key` of an unsettled run returns that run; at the `concurrency` limit (running plus
	 * finishing runs) it rejects `unavailable/busy`. `run` starts after the commit.
	 */
	start(args: A, context: Context, options?: StartOptions): Promise<Run<Outcome<A, R, S>>>;
	/** Waits for the outcome of the unsettled run `id`; a settled or unknown id rejects `gone`. */
	outcome(id: string, context: Context): Promise<Outcome<A, R, S>>;
	/**
	 * Aborts run `id` (D7, as Durable's `abortTask`): marks it (stored for a persisted job) and fires its `run`'s
	 * signal, resolving `"marked"` once its `run` settled (a run not invoked yet ends `aborted` without one); a
	 * finishing run is only marked, a blocked one dropped (no `finish`; its waiters reject `aborted`). `"terminal"` when
	 * no unsettled run has that id. `context` ends only this wait.
	 */
	abort(id: string, context: Context): Promise<"marked" | "terminal">;
	/** The unsettled runs, one entry each in start order, tagged by phase (a JSON watchable, a state member). */
	readonly running: Watchable<readonly RunningEntry<A, S>[]>;
}

## JobImplementation  chord/src/jobs/job.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** What `self.job` takes: the run and the optional finish. */
export type JobImplementation<A, R, S, P extends Principal = Principal> = {
	/** The work, outside transactions; its ctx's abort signal fires on `abort(id)` and on its object's end. */
	readonly run: (args: A, ctx: JobCtx<P, S>) => Promise<R>;
	/** Records the outcome in one transaction (only `await tx.*`); the run's record and state document go with it. */
	readonly finish?: (outcome: Outcome<A, R, S>, tx: Tx) => void | Promise<void>;
};

## RunState  chord/src/jobs/job.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** A run's state document. */
export interface RunState<S> {
	/** The document's value. */
	readonly value: S;
	/**
	 * One transaction on the object's line drafting only this document, under `context` without its abort signal:
	 * admitted while `run` runs (also after an abort, with the run's own ctx), refused `released` once it settled. A
	 * persisted job's change may be `deferred` (D8): adopted and published at once, stored within `withinMs` (1,000 ms by
	 * default) or earlier; a crash loses it. In memory the option changes nothing.
	 */
	change<T>(
		fn: (draft: Draft<S>) => T,
		context: Context,
		options?: { readonly persistence?: CommitPersistence },
	): Promise<T>;
}

used by: chord-effect
/** What `start` and `tx.start` take besides the args. */
export type StartOptions = {
	/** Names one run: a start with the key of an unsettled run returns that run (args not compared). */
	readonly key?: string;
};

## BlockedReason  chord/src/jobs/run.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * Why a run is blocked: its `finish` failed five times in a row, or its version is not the code's (stored by another
 * job version or fingerprint, of a newer version or an older one without an adapter, or of a job the code no longer
 * declares, slice 7b §8).
 */
export type BlockedReason = "finish_failed" | "version";

## Run  chord/src/jobs/run.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** A started run as its caller holds it: its id and a wait for its outcome. */
export interface Run<O> {
	readonly id: string;
	/**
	 * Resolves with the outcome once `finish` committed (also without a `finish`); a blocked run keeps waiting, a dropped
	 * one rejects `aborted`, the object's end rejects with its error; `context` ends only this wait, which then keeps
	 * nothing of it. A rejection's error keeps its stack's receivers (the transaction that ended the run) until its
	 * `stack` is read (V8).
	 */
	outcome(context: Context): Promise<O>;
}

## RunningEntry  chord/src/jobs/running.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * One entry of `running`: a running or finishing run with its args (and state, when the job has a state document), or
 * a blocked run, which carries neither (it may be of another version than the code).
 */
export type RunningEntry<A, S> =
	| ({
			readonly id: string;
			readonly version: number;
			readonly key?: string;
			readonly args: A;
			readonly phase: "running" | "finishing";
	  } & ([S] extends [undefined] ? unknown : { readonly state: S }))
	| { readonly id: string; readonly version: number; readonly phase: "blocked"; readonly reason: BlockedReason };

## JsonRepresentation  chord/src/json.ts
used by: chord-effect; durable-effect via InboxItem
/** Strict-JSON representation of an application data type. Unknown payloads become JsonValue. */
export type JsonRepresentation<T> = IsAny<T> extends true
	? JsonValue
	: unknown extends T
		? JsonValue
		: T extends null | boolean | number | string
			? T
			: T extends readonly (infer TItem)[]
				? JsonRepresentation<TItem>[]
				: T extends object
					? { [TKey in keyof T]: JsonRepresentation<T[TKey]> }
					: never;

## ipcLink  chord/src/link/ipc.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * A link over `port`: each message one `Uint8Array` (V8 serialization keeps it one). It listens from the moment it is
 * made and queues messages until its listener is set, so a child makes it before awaiting its start message; messages
 * that are no `Uint8Array` (the app's own, such as that start message) are not the link's and are skipped. A thrown
 * `send`, an error in its callback or `disconnect` closes the link once; its listeners are removed then.
 */
export function ipcLink(port: IpcPort): Link

## IpcPort  chord/src/link/ipc.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * The part of a Node IPC channel a link uses: a `ChildProcess` or the child's `process`. `send` returning `false` is
 * backpressure (the message is queued by Node), not a failure.
 */
export interface IpcPort {
	send(message: Uint8Array, callback: (error: Error | null) => void): boolean;
	on(event: "message", listener: (message: unknown) => void): unknown;
	on(event: "disconnect", listener: () => void): unknown;
	removeListener(event: "message", listener: (message: unknown) => void): unknown;
	removeListener(event: "disconnect", listener: () => void): unknown;
	disconnect(): void;
	readonly connected: boolean;
}

## Link  chord/src/link/link.ts
used by: chord-effect
// Links (§3): an ordered, bidirectional channel of messages between two hosts, and the in-memory pair.

/** An ordered, bidirectional channel of `Uint8Array` messages between two hosts. Adapters only move bytes. */
export interface Link {
	/** Sends one message; a no-op once closed. */
	send(message: Uint8Array): void;
	/**
	 * Sets the one listener for incoming messages; messages that arrived earlier are delivered to it first. On a closed
	 * link it is not kept.
	 */
	onMessage(listener: (message: Uint8Array) => void): void;
	/** Closes both ends; messages not delivered yet are dropped. */
	close(): void;
	/** Sets the one listener for the close of either end; it runs at once when the link is closed already. */
	onClose(listener: () => void): void;
}

## memoryLinkPair  chord/src/link/link.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** Two ends of one link: what one sends, the other receives asynchronously (a microtask later), in order. */
export function memoryLinkPair(): [Link, Link]

## Codec  chord/src/link/message.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** How a link turns messages into bytes and back; both ends of a link use the same one. */
export interface Codec {
	readonly name: string;
	encode(message: Message): Uint8Array;
	/** Throws on bytes that are no message of this codec (a protocol error); the envelope is checked afterwards. */
	decode(bytes: Uint8Array): Message;
}

## Message  chord/src/link/message.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * A protocol message. `args` absent: a method without arguments; `value` absent: `null`. A `state` entry's `retired`
 * list is read-only (the schema's type is mutable): entries without retirements share `NO_RETIRED`.
 */
export type Message =
	| Exclude<WireMessage, WireState>
	| (Omit<WireState, "holds"> & { readonly holds: readonly StateEntry[] });

## MESSAGE  chord/src/link/message.ts
used by: chord-effect via Message
/** The protocol's messages, one tagged union. Parts are opaque here (the owners parse them). */
const MESSAGE: Schema<{ kind: "hello"; protocol: number; incarnation: string; calls?: number | undefined; } | { kind: "hold"; origin?: number | undefined; hold: number; type: string; version: number; fingerprint: string; params: string | DeflatedPart | Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>; address: { kind: string; params: unknown; }; principal?: { kind: string; } | undefined; incarnation?: string | undefined; chain?: string[] | undefined; limit?: number | undefined; trace?: Record<string, string> | undefined; } | { kind: "release"; origin?: number | undefined; hold: number; } | { kind: "call"; origin?: number | undefined; call: number; hold: number; method: number; args?: string | DeflatedPart | Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike> | undefined; segments?: readonly Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>[] | undefined; trace?: Record<string, string> | undefined; old?: true | undefined; } | { kind: "abort"; origin?: number | undefined; call: number; } | { kind: "retry"; origin?: number | undefined; hold: number; hops: number; } | { kind: "bound"; origin?: number | undefined; }[]; failed: { member: number; error: { kind: "chord"; error: unknown; } | { kind: "plugin"; code: string; message: string; details?: unknown; }; }[]; retired: number[]; }[]; } | { kind: "ack"; origin?: number | undefined; ## Compression  chord/src/link/part.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * A synchronous compressor (`createHost({ compression })`; `nodeCompression` for Node). `deflate` is raw deflate at
 * level 1. `inflate` gives at most `limit` bytes (`Infinity`: no limit; 0 allowed), `too_large` when the output would
 * be larger, `corrupt` for data that is no raw deflate stream.
 */
export interface Compression {
	deflate(bytes: Uint8Array): Uint8Array;
	inflate(bytes: Uint8Array, limit: number): Inflated;
}

	| { readonly kind: "too_large" }
	| { readonly kind: "corrupt"; readonly error: unknown };

## webSocketLink  chord/src/link/websocket.ts

/**
 * A link over `socket`, one binary frame per message (`binaryType = "arraybuffer"`). Messages sent while it connects
 * wait for `open`; a socket closing or closed already gives a closed link; `close` and `error` close the link once, and
 * so does a text frame (no message of this protocol). A frame above the transport's `maxPayload` closes the socket
 * (code 1009), which closes the link.
 */
