## boundOutput  chord/src/output.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * Bound `text` to whole lines within the limits: the first lines for `head`, the last lines for `tail`. The result is an
 * exact slice, trailing newline included. A single line longer than `maxBytes` is cut at the byte limit on a character
 * boundary.
 */
export function boundOutput(text: string, limits: OutputLimits): OutputSlice

## characterEnd  chord/src/output.ts

/** The last character boundary at or before `index`. */

## OutputBuffer  chord/src/output.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * Bounded running output of one stream, such as a tool call's or a process's. Accepting a chunk costs time proportional to the chunk: head retention stops
 * storing once the window is full, and tail retention drops stored text the window no longer needs when it snapshots.
 * Counts of the whole stream are kept so the dropped totals stay exact.
 */
export class OutputBuffer {
	constructor(limits: OutputLimits)
	/** Bytes currently held; bounded by the limits plus one chunk. */
	get storedBytes(): number
	/**
	 * Accept a chunk; returns whether anything was accepted. `skipped` is output omitted right before the chunk, which
	 * must be more than the tail window by at least one byte or line; only tail retention accepts it.
	 */
	push(chunk: string | Uint8Array, skipped?: OutputSkip): boolean
	/** Flush an incomplete trailing character as a replacement character; call when the stream ends. */
	end(): void
	/** Retained, sanitized output and what the limits dropped from the whole stream. */
	snapshot(): BoundedOutput
}

## OutputLimits  chord/src/output.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * Bounded output streams and adaptive progress commits: `OutputBuffer` keeps a head or tail window of a stream at a cost
 * proportional to each chunk, and `Progress` paces commits of a changing value by their size.
 */

/** Retention limits of one output stream. */
export type OutputLimits = { readonly maxBytes: number; readonly maxLines: number; readonly retain: "head" | "tail" };

## OutputSkip  chord/src/output.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * Output a producer omitted before a chunk, measured on the decoded text: every U+FFFD counts as three bytes, and no
 * sanitizing is applied.
 */
export interface OutputSkip {
	/** UTF-8 byte length of the omitted text. */
	readonly bytes: number;
	/** Newlines (U+000A) in the omitted text. */
	readonly newlines: number;
	/** Whether the omitted text ends with a newline. */
	readonly endsWithNewline: boolean;
}

## OutputSlice  chord/src/output.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** An exact slice of the input within the limits, and what it left out. */
export type OutputSlice = {
	readonly text: string;
	readonly bytes: number;
	readonly droppedBytes: number;
	readonly droppedLines: number;
};

## Progress  chord/src/output.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * Adaptive progress commits: the first change after an idle period commits at once; each commit then delays the next
 * by at least `minIntervalMs` and by its written size at 100 KiB/s. At most one commit is in flight; changes made
 * meanwhile coalesce into the next one. Paces on `clock`, by default `Date.now` and `setTimeout`.
 */
export class Progress {
	constructor(
		write: () => Promise<number>,
		onError: (error: unknown) => void,
		minIntervalMs: number,
		clock: ProgressClock = SYSTEM_CLOCK,
	)
	/** Schedule a commit. */
	mark(): void
	/** Schedule a commit; the promise settles with the commit that includes this change. */
	markAndWait(): Promise<void>
	/** Stop committing and wait for the commit in flight; returns the waiters the final commit must settle. */
	async stop(): Promise<PromiseWithResolvers<void>[]>
}

## PROGRESS_BYTES_PER_SECOND  chord/src/output.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** Each progress commit also buys a pause proportional to what it wrote. */
export const PROGRESS_BYTES_PER_SECOND: number

## ProgressClock  chord/src/output.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** The clock and timer progress commits pace on. */
export type ProgressClock = {
	readonly now: () => number;
	/** Call `callback` once after about `delayMs`; returns a function that disarms it. */
	readonly setTimer: (callback: () => void, delayMs: number) => () => void;
};

## RegistryError  chord/src/registries/record.ts
used by: chord-effect via HostError
/** What a registry reports to its host's `onError`, by kind; each once per episode. */
export type RegistryError =
	/** `compose` reported a conflict it resolved. */
	| {
			readonly kind: "registry_conflict";
			readonly registry: string;
			readonly message: string;
			readonly plugins: readonly string[];
	  }
	/** `compose` (or an older version's `value` adapter) threw: the last good composition stays. */
	| { readonly kind: "registry_failed"; readonly registry: string; readonly error: unknown }
	/** A watchable contribution failed or ended, or its `contribution` adapter threw: it is left out until it heals. */
	| {
			readonly kind: "contribution_failed";
			readonly registry: string;
			readonly plugin: string;
			readonly type?: string;
			readonly error: unknown;
	  }
	/** A contribution of a version the provider does not accept (newer, or older without an adapter) is left out. */
	| {
			readonly kind: "contribution_refused";
			readonly registry: string;
			readonly plugin: string;
			readonly type?: string;
			readonly version: number;
	  }
	/**
	 * At a publication, or when a host-lifetime object's contributions enter, the registry has contributions and no
	 * plugin here serves it (`unavailable/undeclared` for its readers): its contributing plugins in table order; again
	 * only once they change.
	 */
	| { readonly kind: "registry_undeclared"; readonly registry: string; readonly plugins: readonly string[] };

export type ComposeContext = {

## Registry  chord/src/registries/registry.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * A registry token: its name (as type names, `[a-z0-9@/._~-]`), the version the bundling plugin was built against, the
 * contribution type `C` and the composed value type `V`. Shared: every contributor and reader bundles its own copy.
 */
export type Registry<C, V> = {
	readonly kind: "registry";
	readonly name: string;
	readonly version: number;
	/** Type only: `C` in, `V` out. */
	readonly "~types"?: (contribution: C) => V;
};

## RegistryAccepts  chord/src/registries/registry.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * Adapters of older versions, by version, the provider's code: `contribution` maps an older contribution to `C` (once
 * per contribution value), `value` maps the composed value back for a reader of that version (once per composition).
 * A plugin annotates the old contribution's type (`(old: HttpV1) => upgrade(old)`).
 */
export type RegistryAccepts<C, V> = {
	readonly [version: number]: {
		readonly contribution?: (old: never) => C;
		readonly value?: (current: V) => unknown;
	};
};

## RegistryConflict  chord/src/registries/registry.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** A conflict `compose` resolved with its fallback: reported as `registry_conflict`, once per conflict episode. */
export type RegistryConflict = { readonly message: string; readonly plugins: readonly string[] };

	/** The contributing object's type; absent for a facet. */

	/** The registry version its contributor was built against (an older one adapted to `C`). */

};

## RegistryProvider  chord/src/registries/registry.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** What the defining plugin's facet serves a registry with (`host.serve(R, provider)`). */
export type RegistryProvider<C, V> = {
	/**
	 * Composes the table: pure and synchronous, always a value (a fallback built in), conflicts reported. Runs when the
	 * table changed and someone reads or follows the value; a throw is the owner's bug (`registry_failed`, the last
	 * good composition stays).
	 */
	readonly compose: (table: RegistryTable<C>, context: ComposeContext) => V;
	readonly accepts?: RegistryAccepts<C, V>;
};

used by: chord-effect
/** A registry's table: one entry per live contributor, sorted by plugin name, then type (a facet's first). */
export type RegistryTable<C> = readonly RegistryEntry<C>[];

## RegistryValue  chord/src/registries/registry.ts
used by: chord-effect; durable-effect via registryReader
/**
 * A registry's composed value as a reader of one version sees it (`self.registry`, `host.registry`): a native
 * watchable; `.value` is the last good composition (a later throwing `compose` keeps it), a watch gets each new one.
 */
export interface RegistryValue<V> extends NativeWatchable<V> {
	/**
	 * A synchronous observer of its compositions (as Durable's `observeXXX`): `advance` runs inside the batch that
	 * composed, so it only records; an attached observer counts as watching, so the composition runs for it.
	 */
	observe(observer: NativeObserver<V>, context: Context): NativeObservation<V>;
}

## SqliteDatabase  chord/src/sqlite/database.ts
used by: chord-effect, durable-effect, durable-rivet-effect
/**
 * Minimal portable SQLite database facade.
 *
 * All operations are asynchronous so adapters may execute outside the caller's runtime.
 *
 * `transaction` passes the callback a transaction handle. All work in the transaction
 * must use that handle; the handle is invalid after the callback settles. Adapters must
 * queue unrelated operations and other transactions until the transaction finishes. The
 * returned promise settles after commit or rollback. Calling the database itself (including
 * `transaction` or `close`) from inside a callback therefore waits for that transaction and
 * never settles.
 *
 * When the callback rejects, the adapter must roll the transaction back before rejecting
 * with that same error. If rollback fails, it must reject with a different error (for
 * example an `AggregateError`) so callers cannot mistake the callback error for a
 * guaranteed rollback.
 */
export interface SqliteDatabase extends SqliteExecutor {
	transaction<T>(callback: (transaction: SqliteExecutor) => Promise<T>): Promise<T>;
	close(): Promise<void>;
}

## SqliteExecutor  chord/src/sqlite/database.ts
used by: chord-effect, durable-effect, durable-rivet-effect
/**
 * Asynchronous SQL operations shared by a database and its transaction handles.
 *
 * `exec` runs SQL text without bindings and may contain several statements. `run`, `get`, and `all`
 * execute one statement with positional bindings. `runCounted` runs one like `run` and resolves with the rows it
 * inserted, updated or deleted, as SQLite's `changes()` counts them (index writes and rows changed by triggers do not
 * count); it may cost a statement more than `run`, so callers that need no count use `run`. Adapters may cache
 * prepared statements by SQL text, so callers pass values as bindings instead of interpolating them.
 */
export interface SqliteExecutor {
	exec(sql: string): Promise<void>;
	run(sql: string, ...params: SqliteValue[]): Promise<void>;
	runCounted(sql: string, ...params: SqliteValue[]): Promise<number>;
	get<T extends object>(sql: string, ...params: SqliteValue[]): Promise<T | undefined>;
	all<T extends object>(sql: string, ...params: SqliteValue[]): Promise<T[]>;
}

## SqliteValue  chord/src/sqlite/database.ts
used by: chord-effect, durable-effect, durable-rivet-effect
/** Values supported by the portable SQLite drivers. */
export type SqliteValue = null | number | bigint | string | Uint8Array;

## NodeSqliteDatabase  chord/src/sqlite/node.ts

export class NodeSqliteDatabase extends NodeSqliteExecutor implements SqliteDatabase {

}

## NodeSqliteDatabaseOptions  chord/src/sqlite/node.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** Node SQLite connection settings for a database file. */
export type NodeSqliteDatabaseOptions = {
	/**
	 * `read-only` opens an existing file for reads (another process may write it): no directory is made, nothing is
	 * configured or checkpointed, and transactions are deferred (`BEGIN`), reading one snapshot. `read-write` by default.
	 */
	readonly mode?: NodeSqliteMode;
	/** SQLite WAL auto-checkpoint threshold. SQLite and this adapter default to 1,000 pages; 0 disables it. */
	readonly walAutoCheckpointPages?: number;
	/** Time SQLite waits for a competing file lock. SQLite defaults to 0; this adapter defaults to 5,000 ms. */
	readonly busyTimeoutMs?: number;
};

## NodeSqliteExecutor  chord/src/sqlite/node.ts
used by: chord-effect via NodeSqliteDatabase
/**
 * Executes SQL on one connection. Prepared statements are cached per connection by SQL text, so the
 * database and its transaction handles share them across transactions. The cache keeps the
 * `STATEMENT_CACHE_LIMIT` most recently used statements, so callers generating SQL of unbounded shapes
 * cannot grow it without bound.
 */
abstract class NodeSqliteExecutor implements SqliteExecutor {
	constructor(database: DatabaseSync, statements: Map<string, StatementSync>)
	exec(sql: string): Promise<void>
	run(sql: string, ...params: SqliteValue[]): Promise<void>
	runCounted(sql: string, ...params: SqliteValue[]): Promise<number>
	get<T extends object>(sql: string, ...params: SqliteValue[]): Promise<T | undefined>
	all<T extends object>(sql: string, ...params: SqliteValue[]): Promise<T[]>
}

## NodeSqliteMode  chord/src/sqlite/node.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** How a connection opens its file. */
export type NodeSqliteMode = "read-write" | "read-only";

export async function openNodeSqliteDatabase(
	path: string,
	options: NodeSqliteDatabaseOptions = {},
): Promise<NodeSqliteDatabase>

## Batch  chord/src/state/batch.ts
used by: chord-effect via ChordStore
/** A host's batch: the reentrancy flag, the watched sources a commit changed, and where background errors go. */
export class Batch {
	/** Reports a throwing watch listener's error (to the host's `onError`); what watches get as their `report`. */
	readonly reportListener: (error: unknown) => void
	constructor(report: (error: BatchError) => void, metrics: TelemetryMetrics | undefined)
	/** Whether a commit's adoption, a delivery or a derive compute runs now: a change made now lands in this batch. */
	get running(): boolean
	/** Throws `invalid/reentrant` inside the batch: `operation` may not run during adoptions or derive computes. */
	assertOutside(operation: string): void
	/**
	 * Throws `invalid/reentrant` inside a pure compute (a derive's, a registry's `compose`): `operation` would change a
	 * source while one is computed from it. Changes inside an adoption are fine (they land in its batch).
	 */
	assertNotComputing(operation: string): void
	/** Runs the pure compute `work` (`run`, and changes refused: `assertNotComputing`); nests. */
	compute<T>(work: () => T): T
	/** Runs `work` with reentrant calls refused; nests (a derive compute inside a commit). */
	run<T>(work: () => T): T
	/**
	 * Runs one commit's adoptions, then, still synchronously, delivers a frame for every watched value they changed
	 * (watched derives recompute through their reads), then runs the flushes the deliveries listed. A delivery or flush
	 * that throws is reported; the others still run. What `within` deferred while the flushes sent runs as the next
	 * commit, right after.
	 */
	commit(adopt: () => void, context: Context): void
	/**
	 * Runs `adopt` inside the commit running now, which delivers what it changed; outside one, as a commit of its own;
	 * while a commit's flushes send, as the next commit (a link closing while it sends ends its holds: their departure
	 * lands in the next batch, so one commit stays one message per link and origin). For changes that happen wherever a
	 * reference binds or ends (`host.references`, `host.activity`).
	 */
	within(adopt: () => void, context: Context): void
	/**
	 * Runs `adopt` in one commit on the next microtask, together with every other `soon` until then (changes arriving
	 * outside any commit, as a followed runtime's calls off its commit step: one batch for all of them). `context` is
	 * the first one's.
	 */
	soon(adopt: () => void, context: Context): void
	/** Lists a watched source the current commit changed. */
	changed(source: Delivered): void
	/** Lists `flush` to run at the end of the current commit, after its deliveries (a link sending what they fed it). */
	flushing(flush: (context: Context) => void): void
	/**
	 * Counts one unit of derive or registry work on the host's metrics (a lazy read has no context to count through).
	 */
	count(
		counter:
			| "chord.derive.computes"
			| "chord.derive.diffs"
			| "chord.registry.composes"
			| "chord.registry.adapts"
			| "chord.contract.adapts",
	): void
}

## BatchError  chord/src/state/batch.ts
used by: chord-effect via HostError
/** What a batch reports: a watch listener that threw, or a frame delivery that threw (a derive's value is no JSON). */
export type BatchError =
	| { readonly kind: "listener_error"; readonly error: unknown }
	| { readonly kind: "delivery_failed"; readonly error: unknown };

## Delivered  chord/src/state/batch.ts
used by: chord-effect via ChordStore
/** What a commit lists to get its frame delivered: a watched source it changed (JSON or native). */
export interface Delivered {
	/** Delivers this batch's frame to its watches and subscribers; called once per batch that listed it. */
	deliver(context: Context): void;
}

## mapShared  chord/src/state/derive.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * Maps an array calling `f` only for object elements not seen before (by identity), returning the previous result for
 * the others; primitive elements are mapped every time. The cache is weak: dropped elements take their results along.
 */
export function mapShared<E, R extends JsonValue>(f: (element: E) => R): (elements: readonly E[]) => R[]

## NativeObservation  chord/src/state/native-source.ts
used by: chord-effect; durable-effect via registryReader
/** What `observe` gives: the value the observer starts at, and how to detach it (Durable's `Observation`). */
export type NativeObservation<T> = { readonly value: T; detach(): void };

## NativeObserver  chord/src/state/native-source.ts
used by: chord-effect; durable-effect via registryReader
/**
 * A synchronous observer of a native source (Durable's observer shape): `advance` is called inside the batch that
 * changed the source, so it only records; `end` once, when the source ended (`ended`) or the observer's context was
 * aborted (`aborted`).
 */
export interface NativeObserver<T> {
	/** The source's call of this batch: its new value, or a failure it may recover from. */
	advance(call: NativeWatchCall<T>, context: Context): void;
	/** The observer is detached for good with `end`. */
	end(end: WatchEnd): void;
}

## constant  chord/src/state/watchable.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** A watchable that never changes (start data, §18); usable as a state member and as a derive source. */
export function constant<const T extends JsonValue>(value: T): Watchable<T>

## Writable  chord/src/state/writable.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** An in-process value that changes when its owner sets it; `set` of the same value notifies nobody. */
export interface Writable<T> extends NativeWatchable<T> {
	/**
	 * Sets the value: a new value (by identity) is a new frame for its watches and marks the derives and registry
	 * tables reading it, in the batch running now or in one of its own. Throws `released` once its attempt ended, and
	 * `invalid/reentrant` inside a derive compute or a `compose`.
	 */
	set(value: T): void;
}

## DecodedRow  chord/src/store/adapter.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** A stored row as reads decode it. */
export type DecodedRow = { readonly [column: string]: unknown };

## OwnerTable  chord/src/store/adapter.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** One declared table of an owner: its rows encoded and written in a step, its reads by key and by query. */
export class OwnerTable {
	readonly definition: TableDefinition
	readonly sql: TableSql
	constructor(definition: TableDefinition, table: string)
	/** `row` checked and encoded for a `put` (a trust boundary, rule 8: at staging, before the queue). */
	encode(row: unknown): EncodedRow
	/**
	 * Writes `encoded` in `step` (an upsert) and returns the `put` as recorded; `stamp` names an `int` column that takes
	 * the step's seq (Durable's `entries.commit_seq`), in the row and in the record.
	 */
	async put(step: Step, encoded: EncodedRow, stamp?: string): Promise<TableWrite>
	/** The row with the key `params` (in key order), decoded. */
	async get(
		executor: Pick<SqliteExecutor, "get">,
		params: readonly SqliteValue[],
		context: Context,
	): Promise<DecodedRow | undefined>
	/**
	 * A read compiled once (the store's query vocabulary rendered to SQL): `columns` of the rows `where` matches in
	 * `order`. The values in `where` only shape it: each is a `?` the caller binds in the order the conditions take
	 * them, then the limit. Adapters keep their fixed reads so: no SQL is rendered per call.
	 */
	prepare(columns: readonly string[], where: WhereNode | undefined, order: Order): string
	/** `prepare` for the first row only: the limit is a literal `1` (a bound one costs SQLite a plan step per call). */
	prepareFirst(columns: readonly string[], where: WhereNode | undefined, order: Order): string
	/**
	 * The version of `json(...)` column `column`: at 1 every stored cell is at 1 (none is older, a newer one fails the
	 * owner when its table is prepared), so a read may leave the version column out.
	 */
	jsonVersion(column: string): number
	/** A point lookup compiled once: `columns` of the row whose key the caller binds, in key order. */
	prepareGet(columns: readonly string[]): string
	/**
	 * The read of `json(...)` column `column`'s stored cells (`text` written at `version`, migrated on access), made
	 * once: an adapter selecting the cell itself reads it so.
	 */
	reader(column: string): (text: string, version: number, context: Context) => unknown
	/** Up to `limit` rows matching `where` in `order`, decoded. */
	async select(
		executor: Pick<SqliteExecutor, "all">,
		where: WhereNode | undefined,
		order: Order,
		limit: number,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<DecodedRow[]>
}

## StoreOwnerTables  chord/src/store/adapter.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * The tables of one owner name in a store: each declared once (its SQL name `"<owner>:<table>"` claimed for
 * `claimant`), then prepared together (created at their newest version or migrated, as `self.table`'s are).
 */
export class StoreOwnerTables {
	readonly store: ChordStore
	readonly owner: string
	/** `owner` is a restricted name (lowercase `[a-z0-9@/._~-]`): it becomes the first part of SQL names. */
	constructor(store: ChordStore, owner: string, claimant: Claimant)
	/** Declares `definition` under the owner, claiming its SQL name (held by another: `invalid/args`). */
	declare(definition: TableDefinition): OwnerTable
	/** Brings every declared table to its definition: created fresh, or migrated eagerly in their commits. */
	prepare(context: Context): Promise<void>
}

## IdAllocator  chord/src/store/allocator.ts
used by: chord-effect via Step
/**
 * The allocator: `value` is the next id it gives. An id raised to `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` is accepted, the value
 * stays there, and every later `mint` throws: no id past the safe range (it would stop counting exactly and repeat).
 */
export class IdAllocator {
	constructor(next: number)
	/** The next id `mint` gives; what each commit persists. */
	get value(): number
	/** Takes the next id; throws "ID space is exhausted" once saturated (Durable's message). */
	mint(): number
	/** Raises the counter above `id`, an id written explicitly (Durable mints ahead), saturating. */
	raise(id: number): void
}

## applyBatch  chord/src/store/apply-batch.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * Applies `commits` (from an outbox, in seq order) to `store`: refused while an owner holds a claim on it, once it
 * diverged, or when the first commit does not follow its `lastSeq` or one does not follow the one before; a write the
 * store's records refuse rolls the whole batch back (`invalid/args`); a recorded count the store does not reproduce
 * rolls it back and marks the store diverged, so every later batch is refused. Commits written to the store's outbox
 * too when it has one.
 */
export function applyBatch(store: ChordStore, commits: readonly OutboxCommit[], context: Context): Promise<void>

## ArchiveManifest  chord/src/store/archive.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * The first part: the format, the store's schema version, its `lastSeq` and the allocator's next id (rule 24, D3);
 * `host` in a host's data archive (`exportHostData`): the address key whose records and rows it holds.
 */
export type ArchiveManifest = {
	readonly kind: "manifest";
	readonly format: number;
	readonly schema: number;
	readonly lastSeq: number;
	readonly nextId: number;
	readonly host?: string;
};

## ArchivePart  chord/src/store/archive.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * One part of an archive, in this order: the manifest; per table (by SQL name) its `table` write, its `put`s and its
 * `index` writes; per document record (by id, live and retired) its `document.create` without a base, then its kept
 * revisions in seq order; `end` with the count of the parts between.
 */
export type ArchivePart =
	| ArchiveManifest
	| Extract<TableWrite, { readonly kind: "table" | "put" | "index" }>
	| Extract<DocumentWrite, { readonly kind: "document.create" | "document.revision" }>
	| { readonly kind: "end"; readonly writes: number };

used by: chord-effect
/** A backend for `openStore` and `importStore`: opaque to apps, owned by the store once given to it. */
export class Backend {
	/** The database the store runs its SQL on. */
	readonly db: SqliteDatabase
	constructor(db: SqliteDatabase)
}

used by: chord-effect
/** A backend over a SQLite database (`openNodeSqliteDatabase(path)`, a Durable Object's storage, `:memory:` in tests). */
export function sqliteBackend(db: SqliteDatabase): Backend

## TableRecord  chord/src/store/catalog.ts
used by: chord-effect via Step
/** A table as the store records it, by its SQL name. */
export type TableRecord = {
	readonly table: string;
	readonly version: number;
	/** `migrating` while an eager migration of `version` runs (slice 6a §9). */
	readonly state: "ready" | "migrating";
	readonly columns: { readonly [name: string]: ColumnRecord };
	readonly key: readonly string[];
	readonly fingerprint: string;
	/** Index definitions by name: their declared columns (the key is appended when rendered). */
	readonly indexes: { readonly [name: string]: readonly string[] };
};

## Claimant  chord/src/store/claims.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** Who holds claims: named in the refusal of a second claim. */
export type Claimant = { readonly label: string };

## ColumnSet  chord/src/store/column-set.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * A declared column set: its columns, key and indexes, checked once here. `refs` are its column references, for
 * conditions over the set wherever it appears (a query's own table, a joined set, an `exists`).
 */
export class ColumnSet<C extends Columns = Columns, K extends readonly string[] = readonly string[]> {
	readonly name: string
	/** The column schemas as declared: what a table spreads into its own columns. */
	readonly columns: C
	readonly byName: ReadonlyMap<string, Column>
	readonly key: readonly string[]
	readonly indexes: ReadonlyMap<string, readonly string[]>
	readonly refs: ColumnRefs<C>
	/** Type only: the key. */
	declare readonly "~key"?: K
	constructor(name: string, options: ColumnSetOptions<C, K & readonly OrderColumn<C>[]>)
}

## ColumnSetOptions  chord/src/store/column-set.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** What `defineColumns` takes. */
export type ColumnSetOptions<C extends Columns, K extends readonly OrderColumn<C>[]> = {
	/** The public columns: scalar ones (`str int num bool`, `opt(...)` of them, `host(...)`). */
	readonly columns: C;
	/** The key of the table that exposes the set. */
	readonly key: K;
	/** The indexes others may match by, each a leading prefix of one of the table's. */
	readonly indexes?: { readonly [name: string]: readonly OrderColumn<C>[] };
};

## defineColumns  chord/src/store/column-set.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** Declares the columns of a table that other plugins' conditions and joins may read. */
export function defineColumns<C extends Columns, const K extends readonly OrderColumn<C>[]>(
	name: string,
	options: ColumnSetOptions<C, K>,
): ColumnSet<C, K>

## Column  chord/src/store/columns.ts
used by: chord-effect via ColumnSet
/**
 * A column of the store: its name, type, nullability and default; a `json(...)` one with its definition; a `host(...)`
 * one is a non-`opt` `str` column with its `host` definition.
 */
export type Column =
	| {
			readonly name: string;
			readonly type: "str" | "int" | "num" | "bool";
			readonly optional: boolean;
			readonly default: string | number | boolean | undefined;
			readonly host?: HostColumn;
	  }
	| { readonly name: string; readonly type: "json"; readonly optional: boolean; readonly json: JsonColumn };

## ColumnRecord  chord/src/store/columns.ts
used by: chord-effect via TableDefinition
/** A column as the `table` write records it (slice 6a §5): what a replica needs without the plugin's code. */
export type ColumnRecord = {
	readonly type: ColumnType;
	readonly optional?: true;
	readonly default?: string | number | boolean;
	/** A `json(...)` column's version and schema fingerprint. */
	readonly version?: number;
	readonly fingerprint?: string;
	/** A `host(...)` column's host kind (a `str` column holding its address keys). */
	readonly host?: string;
};

## Columns  chord/src/store/columns.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** A table's `columns`: a flat record of column schemas. */
export type Columns = { readonly [name: string]: ColumnSchema };

## ColumnSchema  chord/src/store/columns.ts
used by: chord-effect via Columns
/** A schema a table column takes. */
export type ColumnSchema =
	| ScalarSchema
	| JsonColumnSchema<unknown>
	| HostColumnSchema<KindShape>
	| Optional<ScalarSchema | JsonColumnSchema<unknown>>;

## ColumnType  chord/src/store/columns.ts
used by: chord-effect via ColumnRef
/** A column's type in the store. */
export type ColumnType = "str" | "int" | "num" | "bool" | "json";

## ColumnTypeOf  chord/src/store/columns.ts
used by: chord-effect via Match
/** The store type of column schema `S` (a `host(...)` column is a `str` one holding address keys). */
export type ColumnTypeOf<S> = S extends Optional<infer I>
	? ColumnTypeOf<I>
	: S extends HostColumnSchema<KindShape>
		? "str"
		: S extends StringSchema
			? "str"
			: S extends IntegerSchema
				? "int"
				: S extends NumberSchema
					? "num"
					: S extends BooleanSchema
						? "bool"
						: "json";

## DefaultedNames  chord/src/store/columns.ts
used by: chord-effect via PutRowOf
/** The names of the columns with a declared default. */
type DefaultedNames<C extends Columns> = {
	[K in keyof C]: C[K] extends { readonly default: unknown } ? K : never;
}[keyof C];

## HostColumnOf  chord/src/store/columns.ts
used by: chord-effect via TableDefinition
/** A `host(...)` column: a non-`opt` `str` column with its definition. */
export type HostColumnOf = ScalarColumn & { readonly type: "str"; readonly host: HostColumn };

## OrderColumn  chord/src/store/columns.ts
used by: chord-effect via ColumnSet
/** The columns a key, an index or an `orderBy` may use: non-`opt` `str`, `int` or `host(...)`. */
export type OrderColumn<C extends Columns> = {
	[K in keyof C]: C[K] extends Optional
		? never
		: C[K] extends StringSchema | IntegerSchema | HostColumnSchema<KindShape>
			? K
			: never;
}[keyof C] &
	string;

## PutRowOf  chord/src/store/columns.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** A row as `put` takes it: as read, the columns with a default may be left out (rule 15). */
export type PutRowOf<C extends Columns> = { [K in Exclude<RequiredNames<C>, DefaultedNames<C>>]: ValueOf<C[K]> } & {
	[K in Exclude<keyof C, Exclude<RequiredNames<C>, DefaultedNames<C>>>]?: ValueOf<C[K]>;
};

## RequiredNames  chord/src/store/columns.ts
used by: chord-effect via PutRowOf
/** The names of the columns that are not `opt(...)`. */
type RequiredNames<C extends Columns> = { [K in keyof C]: C[K] extends Optional ? never : K }[keyof C];

## RowOf  chord/src/store/columns.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** A row as reads return it: every non-`opt` column, the `opt(...)` ones when not `NULL`. */
export type RowOf<C extends Columns> = { [K in RequiredNames<C>]: ValueOf<C[K]> } & {
	[K in Exclude<keyof C, RequiredNames<C>>]?: ValueOf<C[K]>;
};

## ScalarColumn  chord/src/store/columns.ts
used by: chord-effect via TableDefinition
/** A column that is not `json(...)`: a scalar one, a `host(...)` one among them. */
export type ScalarColumn = Exclude<Column, { readonly type: "json" }>;

## ScalarSchema  chord/src/store/columns.ts
used by: chord-effect via Columns
type ScalarSchema = StringSchema | IntegerSchema | NumberSchema | BooleanSchema;

## ValueOf  chord/src/store/columns.ts
used by: chord-effect via PutRowOf
/** The value type of column schema `S` (without `undefined` for an `opt(...)` one). */
export type ValueOf<S> = S extends Optional<infer I> ? ValueOf<I> : S extends Schema ? Static<S> : never;

## DocumentAddress  chord/src/store/engine.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * A document's address: the owner name, the adapter's namespace (claimed with the owner: Chord's `chord`, `chord.jobs`,
 * `chord.job-states`; Durable's scopes), the kind and, for a keyed document, its key; a singleton has none. The column
 * keeps `""` for it, which a keyed document's empty key shares (its definition says which it is).
 */
export type DocumentAddress = {
	readonly owner: string;
	readonly namespace: string;
	readonly kind: string;
	readonly key?: string;
};

## DocumentBase  chord/src/store/engine.ts
used by: chord-effect via DocumentContent
/** A base: a whole value at a version. */
export type DocumentBase = { readonly version: number; readonly fingerprint: string; readonly value: JsonValue };

## DocumentContent  chord/src/store/engine.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** A change's content: a new base, or a delta on the current base's version. */
export type DocumentContent =
	| ({ readonly kind: "base" } & DocumentBase)
	| { readonly kind: "delta"; readonly version: number; readonly ops: readonly Op[] };

## DocumentEntry  chord/src/store/engine.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * A record as an adapter that keeps its own fields in `meta` reads it: the meta, and, where a read can find retired
 * records (at a point, by id), when it was retired. One or two columns: each column a read returns costs.
 */
export type DocumentEntry = { readonly meta: string | null; readonly retired_at?: number | null };

## DocumentHistory  chord/src/store/engine.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * What a record keeps (R1), applied at a new base and at retirement: `none` (Chord) drops older revisions at a new base
 * and the row and its revisions at retirement; `latest` drops older revisions at a new base and its revisions at
 * retirement, keeping the row; `rewindable` keeps everything.
 */
export type DocumentHistory = "none" | "latest" | "rewindable";

## DocumentPoint  chord/src/store/engine.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** Where a read looks: the current state, or the state after a seq. */
export type DocumentPoint = number | "current";

## DocumentRecord  chord/src/store/engine.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** A stored record: one incarnation of an address, live from `createdAt` until `retiredAt` (half-open). */
export type DocumentRecord = DocumentAddress & {
	readonly id: number;
	readonly history: DocumentHistory;
	/** The seq that created it. */
	readonly createdAt: number;
	/** The seq that retired it, once retired. */
	readonly retiredAt?: number;
	/** The adapter's details (Durable: its fork policy and history). */
	readonly meta?: string;
	/** The address key of the host it belongs to (Chord's host-keyed documents, schema 3); absent for others. */
	readonly host?: string;
	/** Counts its changes: a change names the revision it was prepared on. */
	readonly revision: number;
	/** The version and schema fingerprint of its current base. */
	readonly version: number;
	readonly fingerprint: string;
};

## DocumentRevision  chord/src/store/engine.ts
used by: chord-effect via ArchivePart
/** One stored revision as archives carry it: its document, its seq, its content. */
export type DocumentRevision = { readonly id: number; readonly seq: number; readonly content: RevisionContent };

## DocumentScope  chord/src/store/engine.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** What `listDocuments` scans: one owner's namespace, optionally one kind. */
export type DocumentScope = { readonly owner: string; readonly namespace: string; readonly kind?: string };

## DocumentWrite  chord/src/store/engine.ts
used by: chord-effect via ArchivePart
/**
 * The engine's writes as the outbox and archives record them. A creation carries its base in a commit (stored at
 * `createdAt`); in an archive it has none and its `document.revision`s follow it.
 */
export type DocumentWrite =
	| { readonly kind: "document.create"; readonly record: DocumentRecord; readonly base?: DocumentBase }
	| {
			readonly kind: "document.change";
			readonly id: number;
			readonly revision: number;
			readonly content: DocumentContent;
	  }
	| { readonly kind: "document.retire"; readonly id: number; readonly revision: number }
	| ({ readonly kind: "document.revision" } & DocumentRevision);

/**
 * Loads `record` at `at`: its newest base at or below it and the deltas after that base up to it, applied once; the

 * Retires live `record` in the step's seq by its history (R1): a `none` record's row and revisions go, a `latest` one
 * keeps its row with `retired_at` and drops its revisions, a `rewindable` one keeps everything.

## RevisionContent  chord/src/store/engine.ts
used by: chord-effect via ArchivePart
/** A stored revision's content: a base's value or a delta's ops, at a version (a revision keeps no fingerprint). */
export type RevisionContent =
	| { readonly kind: "base"; readonly version: number; readonly value: JsonValue }
	| { readonly kind: "delta"; readonly version: number; readonly ops: readonly Op[] };

## StoredDocument  chord/src/store/engine.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** A loaded document: its record and its value (a base plus deltas applied once) at a point. */
export type StoredDocument = {
	readonly record: DocumentRecord;
	readonly value: JsonValue;
	/** The version of the base the value was built from. */
	readonly version: number;
	/** The deltas applied after its base (what `checkpointWhen` sees). */

};

## writeContent  chord/src/store/engine.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * Writes `content` to document `id` (of `history`) prepared on `revision`, in the step's seq: its revision, the
 * counted conditional `UPDATE` (a delta only on the base's version), and at a new base the older revisions a
 * `none` or `latest` record drops. A record that is not live at `revision` throws (memory and disk disagree).
 */
export async function writeContent(
	step: Step,
	id: number,
	history: DocumentHistory,
	revision: number,
	content: DocumentContent,
	text: string,
): Promise<void>

## ColumnRef  chord/src/store/expression.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * A reference to a column of the row, as `(t) => …` callbacks get them. One of a column set (`Set.refs`) carries the
 * set's name: a condition names the side it means by it (a query's own table, a joined set, an `exists`).
 */
export class ColumnRef<T = unknown, K extends ColumnType = ColumnType> extends Expression<T, K> {
	readonly column: string
	readonly set: string | undefined
	constructor(column: string, set?: string)
}

## Comparable  chord/src/store/expression.ts
used by: chord-effect via eq
/** A value `eq`, `ne` and `inArray` compare a column with: a scalar, or an address for a `host(...)` column. */
type Comparable = Scalar | Address;

## Comparison  chord/src/store/expression.ts
used by: chord-effect via Condition
/** The comparison operators of a `WhereNode`. */
export type Comparison = "eq" | "ne" | "lt" | "lte" | "gt" | "gte";

## compile  chord/src/store/expression.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** A condition over `set`'s columns as plain data (slice 14 §6), for `whereNode` and `existsNode`. */
export function compile(set: ColumnSet, condition: Condition): WhereNode

## concat  chord/src/store/expression.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** `a` followed by `b`. */
export function concat(a: Operand<string, "str">, b: Operand<string, "str">): Expression<string, "str">

## Condition  chord/src/store/expression.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** A condition as a plugin builds it; compiled when staged or run. */
export class Condition {
	readonly op: Comparison | "inArray" | "isNull" | "prefix" | "and" | "or" | "not" | "exists" | "existsNode"
	readonly args: readonly unknown[]
	constructor(op: Condition["op"], args: readonly unknown[])
}

## eq  chord/src/store/expression.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** The column equals `value` (`NULL` never matches). */
export function eq<T extends Comparable>(column: ColumnRef<T, ScalarType>, value: T): Condition

## exists  chord/src/store/expression.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * `set`'s table has a row equal to the enclosing row in the matched columns (a leading prefix of the set's key or of
 * one of its declared indexes) that satisfies `inner`. In queries only.
 */
export function exists<C extends Columns>(
	set: ColumnSet<C>,
	match: Match<C>,
	inner?: (row: ColumnSet<C>["refs"]) => Condition,
): Condition

## existsNode  chord/src/store/expression.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * `exists` with its inner condition as data (`compile`'s result): for a condition handed over as an argument. A
 * trust boundary: `inner` is whatever arrived, and is checked whole before anything is rendered.
 */
export function existsNode<C extends Columns>(set: ColumnSet<C>, match: Match<C>, inner: unknown): Condition

## ExistsNode  chord/src/store/expression.ts
used by: chord-effect via WhereNode
/** The data of an `exists`: the set's name, the matched pairs (set column, enclosing column), the inner condition. */
export type ExistsNode = readonly [string, readonly (readonly [string, string])[], WhereNode | null];

## Expression  chord/src/store/expression.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** A value expression as a plugin builds it: `T` is its value, `K` its column type. Compiled when staged. */
export class Expression<T = unknown, K extends ColumnType = ColumnType> {
	readonly op: Operation | "col"
	readonly args: readonly unknown[]
	/** Type only. */
	declare readonly "~value"?: T
	declare readonly "~type"?: K
	constructor(op: Operation | "col", args: readonly unknown[])
}

## ExprNode  chord/src/store/expression.ts
used by: chord-effect via OwnerTable
/**
 * A compiled value expression: a literal (`null` clears), a column, a `json(...)` cell, or an operation. Untagged on
 * purpose, as `WhereNode`: the stored format.
 */
export type ExprNode =
	| Scalar
	| null
	| { readonly col: string }
	| { readonly json: JsonValue }
	| { readonly add: readonly [ExprNode, ExprNode] }
	| { readonly sub: readonly [ExprNode, ExprNode] }
	| { readonly max: readonly [ExprNode, ExprNode] }
	| { readonly min: readonly [ExprNode, ExprNode] }
	| { readonly concat: readonly [ExprNode, ExprNode] }
	| { readonly coalesce: readonly [ExprNode, ExprNode] }
	| { readonly replacePrefix: readonly [ExprNode, string, string] }
	| { readonly when: readonly [WhereNode, ExprNode, ExprNode] };

## gt  chord/src/store/expression.ts

/** The column is above `value`. */
export function gt<T extends Scalar>(column: ColumnRef<T, ScalarType>, value: T): Condition

## gte  chord/src/store/expression.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** The column is at least `value`. */
export function gte<T extends Scalar>(column: ColumnRef<T, ScalarType>, value: T): Condition

## inArray  chord/src/store/expression.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** The column equals one of `values` (`[]` matches nothing). */
export function inArray<T extends Comparable>(column: ColumnRef<T, ScalarType>, values: readonly T[]): Condition

used by: chord-effect
/** The column is `NULL` (an `opt(...)` column without a value). */
export function isNull(column: ColumnRef<unknown, ScalarType>): Condition

## lt  chord/src/store/expression.ts

/** The column is below `value`. */
export function lt<T extends Scalar>(column: ColumnRef<T, ScalarType>, value: T): Condition

## lte  chord/src/store/expression.ts

/** The column is at most `value`. */
export function lte<T extends Scalar>(column: ColumnRef<T, ScalarType>, value: T): Condition

## Match  chord/src/store/expression.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** The columns of a set matched to columns of the enclosing row: `{ setColumn: column }`. */
export type Match<C extends Columns> = {
	readonly [P in keyof C & string]?: ColumnRef<ValueOf<C[P]>, ColumnTypeOf<C[P]>>;
};

export function ne<T extends Comparable>(column: ColumnRef<T, ScalarType>, value: T): Condition

/** The condition does not hold (`NULL` stays `NULL`: it never matches). */
export function not(condition: Condition): Condition

## Operand  chord/src/store/expression.ts
used by: chord-effect via add
/** An operand of type `T` and column type `K`: an expression or a plain value. */
type Operand<T, K extends ColumnType> = Expression<T, K> | T;

## Operation  chord/src/store/expression.ts
used by: chord-effect via Expression
/** The operations of an `ExprNode`. */
export type Operation = "add" | "sub" | "max" | "min" | "concat" | "coalesce" | "replacePrefix" | "when";

/** Some condition holds (`or()` never does). */
export function or(...conditions: Condition[]): Condition

/** `value` with its prefix `from` replaced by `to`; a value without the prefix stays as it is. */
export function replacePrefix(value: Operand<string, "str">, from: string, to: string): Expression<string, "str">

/** A scalar column type. */
type ScalarType = Exclude<ColumnType, "json">;

## SetNode  chord/src/store/expression.ts
used by: chord-effect via OwnerTable
/** A compiled `set`: the new value of each changed column, every right side evaluated against the row before. */
export type SetNode = { readonly [column: string]: ExprNode };

## SetOf  chord/src/store/expression.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * A `set` of a table with columns `C` and key `K`: new values of non-key columns, each a value or an expression of
 * the column's type; `undefined` clears an `opt(...)` column.
 */
export type SetOf<C extends Columns, K extends readonly string[]> = {
	readonly [P in Exclude<keyof C & string, K[number]>]?: C[P] extends Optional
		? ValueOf<C[P]> | Expression<ValueOf<C[P]>, ColumnTypeOf<C[P]>> | undefined
		: ValueOf<C[P]> | Expression<ValueOf<C[P]>, ColumnTypeOf<C[P]>>;
};

## sub  chord/src/store/expression.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** `a - b` over integers; a result outside ±(2^53 - 1) fails (rule 10). */
export function sub(a: Operand<number, "int">, b: Operand<number, "int">): Expression<number, "int">

## when  chord/src/store/expression.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** `a` where `condition` holds for the row, else `b`. */
export function when<T, K extends ScalarType>(
	condition: Condition,
	a: Operand<T, K>,
	b: Operand<T, K>,
): Expression<T, K>

## WhereNode  chord/src/store/expression.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * A compiled condition: column comparisons with checked operands, combined by `and`, `or`, `not`. A query's
 * condition may also test `exists` (slice 14 §5): `[set, [[setColumn, column], …], inner]`, true for a row when the
 * set's table has a row equal in the matched columns that satisfies `inner`. Writes take no `exists`. Untagged on
 * purpose: each node is told apart by its one key (`"and" in node`), as the stored format (outbox, archives) holds it.
 */
export type WhereNode =
	| { readonly eq: readonly [string, Scalar] }
	| { readonly ne: readonly [string, Scalar] }
	| { readonly lt: readonly [string, Scalar] }
	| { readonly lte: readonly [string, Scalar] }
	| { readonly gt: readonly [string, Scalar] }
	| { readonly gte: readonly [string, Scalar] }
	| { readonly inArray: readonly [string, readonly Scalar[]] }
	| { readonly isNull: string }
	| { readonly prefix: readonly [string, string] }
	| { readonly and: readonly WhereNode[] }
	| { readonly or: readonly WhereNode[] }
	| { readonly not: WhereNode }
	| { readonly exists: ExistsNode };

## host  chord/src/store/host-column.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** A column holding an address of host kind `kind` per row: the row belongs to that host. */
export function host<N extends string, P extends Params>(kind: HostKind<N, P>): HostColumnSchema<HostKind<N, P>>

## HostColumn  chord/src/store/host-column.ts
used by: chord-effect via HostColumnSchema
/** A `host(...)` column's definition: its kind, the stored key of an address and the address of a stored key. */
export class HostColumn {
	readonly kind: KindShape
	constructor(kind: KindShape)
	/**
	 * The canonical stored key of `value`, an address of the column's kind (a trust boundary): its key under the `str()`
	 * text rules (a lone surrogate replaced, NUL refused), as document keys and host data selections have it;
	 * `invalid/args` otherwise.
	 */
	key(value: unknown, what: string): string
	/** The address a stored key holds. */
	address(key: string): Address
}

## HostColumnSchema  chord/src/store/host-column.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** A `host(...)` column as `columns` takes it: a schema of the kind's addresses carrying the column. */
export interface HostColumnSchema<K extends KindShape> extends Schema<Address<K>> {
	readonly host: HostColumn;
}

used by: chord-effect
/**
 * The records and rows of `store` belonging to `address` as archive parts (manifest with `host`, the tables with a
 * `host(...)` column of its kind and only its rows, its records), holding the commit queue as `store.export` does.
 */
export function exportHostData(store: Store, address: Address, context: Context): AsyncIterableIterator<ArchivePart>

## HostArchive  chord/src/store/host-data.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** A host's data archive, read and checked (`readHostArchive`): one archive is one commit, so it is held in memory. */
export type HostArchive = {
	/** The address key whose data it holds (its manifest's `host`). */
	readonly host: string;
	readonly tables: readonly HostTable[];
	readonly documents: readonly HostDocument[];
};

## HostDataCounts  chord/src/store/host-data.ts

export type HostDataCounts = { readonly documents: number; readonly rows: number };

## HostDocument  chord/src/store/host-data.ts
used by: chord-effect via HostArchive
/** One document of a host's data archive: its record and its value (its base with its deltas applied). */
type HostDocument = { readonly record: DocumentRecord; readonly value: JsonValue };

## HostImportOptions  chord/src/store/host-data.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** What the host's `importHostData` takes besides the kind, the archive and the context. */
export type HostImportOptions = {
	/** The address the data is imported under: a copy when it is not the archive's; another kind is refused. */
	readonly address?: Address;
	/** What happens when the store has data of the address: refused (the default), or replaced in the same commit. */
	readonly existing?: "refuse" | "replace";
};

## HostTable  chord/src/store/host-data.ts
used by: chord-effect via HostArchive
/** One table of a host's data archive: its `table` write, its host column, the `put`s of the host's rows, its indexes. */
export type HostTable = {
	readonly write: Extract<TableWrite, { readonly kind: "table" }>;
	readonly column: string;
	readonly puts: Extract<TableWrite, { readonly kind: "put" }>[];
	readonly indexes: Extract<TableWrite, { readonly kind: "index" }>[];
};

## readHostArchive  chord/src/store/host-data.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * Reads and checks a host's data archive (a trust boundary): every part by the archive schema and in archive order;
 * a manifest with `host` (well-formed text); tables with exactly one host column of that address's kind; every row's host cell and every
 * record's `host` and key the manifest's `host`; live Chord records (history `none`) whose revisions start at a base,
 * each delta at its base's version; `end` counting the parts between. `invalid/args` otherwise.
 */
export async function readHostArchive(
	parts: AsyncIterable<unknown> | Iterable<unknown>,
	context: Context,
): Promise<HostArchive>

## importStore  chord/src/store/import.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * A store holding the archive `parts` on `backend`, which must not hold a store yet: at the manifest's `lastSeq`, its
 * outbox (when `options.outbox`) starting after it. A refused archive, a stalled input cancelled by `context` or a
 * backend error rejects; the backend is closed then (rule 12).
 */
export async function importStore(
	backend: Backend,
	parts: AsyncIterable<unknown> | Iterable<unknown>,
	context: Context,
	options: StoreOptions = {},
): Promise<Store>

## json  chord/src/store/json-column.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** A column holding one JSON value of `schema` per row, at `version`; wrap it in `opt(...)` to make it nullable. */
export function json<S extends Schema>(schema: S, options: JsonColumnOptions<Static<S>>): JsonColumnSchema<Static<S>>

## JsonColumn  chord/src/store/json-column.ts
used by: chord-effect via JsonColumnSchema
/** A `json(...)` column's definition: its schema snapshot, version and fingerprint, and the read of a stored cell. */
export class JsonColumn {
	readonly schema: JsonSchema
	readonly version: number
	/** The fingerprint of the schema's normal form, recorded with the table: the same version with another is `broken`. */
	readonly fingerprint: string
	constructor(schema: Schema, version: number, migrate: ((old: JsonValue, from: number) => unknown) | undefined)
	/**
	 * The value of a stored cell written at `version`: parsed; an older one migrated and checked once (R8, counted). A
	 * newer version, a missing or throwing `migrate` and an invalid result throw `unavailable` (`what` names the cell);
	 * the caller fails the owner (slice 6a §1.4), the data stays.
	 */
	read(text: string, version: number, what: string, context: Context): unknown
}

## JsonColumnOptions  chord/src/store/json-column.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** What `json(...)` takes besides the schema. */
export type JsonColumnOptions<T> = {
	/** The version of the cells' shape; a cell stores the version it was written at. */
	readonly version: number;
	/** Maps a cell of an older version `from` to this version's shape; pure. Without it older cells are refused. */
	readonly migrate?: (old: JsonValue, from: number) => T;
};

## JsonColumnSchema  chord/src/store/json-column.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** A `json(...)` column as `columns` takes it: a schema of the cells' type carrying the column. */
export interface JsonColumnSchema<T> extends Schema<T> {
	readonly json: JsonColumn;
}

## decodeJsonl  chord/src/store/jsonl.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * The values of JSONL `bytes`, one per nonempty line, for `importStore` to check (a trust boundary: bytes that are
 * no UTF-8 and a line that is no JSON are `invalid/args`).
 */
export async function* decodeJsonl(bytes: AsyncIterable<Uint8Array>): AsyncIterable<unknown>

## encodeJsonl  chord/src/store/jsonl.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** `parts` as JSONL bytes, in chunks of whole lines. */
export async function* encodeJsonl(parts: AsyncIterable<ArchivePart>): AsyncIterable<Uint8Array>

## Outbox  chord/src/store/outbox.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** A store's outbox: its commits after the floor (the seq it was turned on at, advanced by `trim`). */
export class Outbox {
	constructor(store: ChordStore, floor: number)
	/** The seq the outbox starts after: `read` takes any `afterSeq` from it to `lastSeq`. */
	get floor(): number
	/** Up to `limit` commits after `afterSeq`, in seq order; `afterSeq` outside floor..lastSeq is `invalid/args`. */
	async read(afterSeq: number, limit: number, context: Context): Promise<OutboxCommit[]>
	/**
	 * Drops the commits through `throughSeq` and advances the floor; idempotent; beyond `lastSeq` is `invalid/args`.
	 * Trims run one at a time, so the stored floor only rises and equals the one in memory.
	 */
	trim(throughSeq: number, context: Context): Promise<void>
}

## OutboxCommit  chord/src/store/outbox.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** One commit as the outbox gives it: its seq, the allocator's value it persisted (D3) and its writes in applied order. */
export type OutboxCommit = { readonly seq: number; readonly nextId: number; readonly writes: readonly StoreWrite[] };

## ColumnRefs  chord/src/store/query.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** The column references a table's callbacks get: `e.path`, `e.at`. */
export type ColumnRefs<C extends Columns> = {
	readonly [K in keyof C & string]: ColumnRef<ValueOf<C[K]>, ColumnTypeOf<C[K]>>;
};

## Joined  chord/src/store/query.ts
used by: chord-effect via Query
/** The set a query joins: one row of it per own row, by the set's whole key. */
export type Joined = {
	readonly set: ColumnSet;
	/** The set's key columns and the own columns each is matched to, in key order. */
	readonly pairs: readonly (readonly [string, string])[];
};

## NoColumns  chord/src/store/query.ts
used by: chord-effect via Query
/** No joined set: a query's partner references are empty then. */
export type NoColumns = Record<never, never>;

## query  chord/src/store/query.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** A query of `table`: its rows, in key order. */
export function query<C extends Columns, K extends readonly string[]>(table: TableDefinition<C, K>): Query<C, K>

## Query  chord/src/store/query.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * An immutable query of one table: an optional condition (several `where`s are `and`ed), an order (`orderBy`
 * columns, one direction, the key appended unless already there) and at most one joined set, whose columns (`J`) the
 * condition and the order may use too.
 */
export class Query<
	C extends Columns = Columns,
	K extends readonly string[] = readonly string[],
	J extends Columns = NoColumns,
> {
	readonly table: TableDefinition<C, K>
	readonly condition: WhereNode | undefined
	readonly joined: Joined | undefined
	/** The set columns its `exists` were written for (`Expected`): checked when a read of it opens. */
	readonly expected: ReadonlyMap<string, ReadonlyMap<string, Column>>
	constructor(
		table: TableDefinition<C, K>,
		condition: WhereNode | undefined,
		orderBy: readonly string[],
		direction: "asc" | "desc" | undefined,
		joined: Joined | undefined,
		expected: ReadonlyMap<string, ReadonlyMap<string, Column>>,
	)
	/** This query with `fn`'s condition too; `partner` are the joined set's columns. */
	where(fn: (row: ColumnRefs<C>, partner: ColumnRefs<J>) => Condition): Query<C, K, J>
	/**
	 * This query with a condition handed over as data (`compile(set, …)`, slice 14 §6): over the own table when it
	 * exposes `set`, over the partner when `set` is joined. A trust boundary: `node` is whatever arrived as an
	 * argument, and the whole of it is checked first.
	 */
	whereNode(set: ColumnSet, node: unknown): Query<C, K, J>
	/**
	 * This query joined with the one row of `set` whose key equals `match`'s own columns: an inner join driven from
	 * the own table. The match covers the set's whole key; one set per query, and not the one the table exposes.
	 */
	join<S extends Columns>(set: ColumnSet<S>, match: (row: ColumnRefs<C>) => Match<S>): Query<C, K, S>
	/**
	 * This query ordered by `fn`'s column next (a non-`opt` `str` or `int` one, of the table or of the joined set), in
	 * `direction`: one direction per query, no column twice (`invalid/args`).
	 */
	orderBy(
		fn: (row: ColumnRefs<C>, partner: ColumnRefs<J>) => ColumnRef<unknown, "str" | "int">,
		direction: "asc" | "desc" = "asc",
	): Query<C, K, J>
	/** The order of its rows: the `orderBy` columns, then the key columns not among them. */
	get order(): Order
	/** The column `name` of its order or condition: the table's, or the joined set's (`<set>:<column>`). */
	column(name: string): Column | undefined
}

## EncodedKey  chord/src/store/rows.ts
used by: chord-effect via TableDefinition
/** A key ready for the store: its parameters in key order, its record and its identity within one table. */
export type EncodedKey = {
	readonly params: readonly SqliteValue[];
	readonly key: { readonly [column: string]: Scalar };
	/** `JSON.stringify` of the parameters: equal keys, equal ids. */
	readonly id: string;
};

## EncodedRow  chord/src/store/rows.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** A `put` ready for the step: its parameters in `physical` order and its record. */
export type EncodedRow = {
	readonly params: readonly SqliteValue[];
	readonly row: StoredRow;
	/** Each written `json(...)` column's version. */
	readonly columns: { readonly [column: string]: number };
	/** The row's key identity, as `EncodedKey.id`. */
	readonly id: string;
};

## RowCodec  chord/src/store/rows.ts
used by: chord-effect via TableDefinition
/**
 * A table version's codec: `put` rows and keys checked and encoded, stored rows decoded. `physical` is the column
 * order of an encoded row (`physicalColumns`).
 */
export class RowCodec {
	readonly physical: readonly string[]
	constructor(columns: readonly Column[], key: readonly string[], table: string)
	/**
	 * Checks and encodes a `put` row of table version `version` (a trust boundary): a plain object with every
	 * non-`opt` column (a defaulted one filled in) and no other field; `invalid/args` otherwise.
	 */
	put(row: unknown, version: number): EncodedRow
	/** Checks and encodes a key (a trust boundary): an object with exactly the key columns; `invalid/args` otherwise. */
	key(key: unknown, what: string): EncodedKey
	/**
	 * A stored row as reads return it: booleans from 0 and 1, `opt(...)` columns absent when `NULL`, `json(...)` cells
	 * parsed and migrated on access (a cell the code cannot read throws, see `JsonColumn.read`).
	 */
	decode(stored: { readonly [column: string]: SqliteValue }, context: Context): { [column: string]: unknown }
	/**
	 * A row as reads return it with its `host(...)` cell as stored (the address's key), for the evaluator, which
	 * compares stored values; the row itself without a host column.
	 */
	stored<R extends { readonly [column: string]: unknown }>(row: R): R
	/** A row with its `host(...)` cell as stored (a key) turned into the address reads return; `stored`'s inverse. */
	addressed<R extends { readonly [column: string]: unknown }>(row: R): R
}

## Scalar  chord/src/store/rows.ts

/** A scalar cell as the store keeps it in rows, writes and operands: a well-formed string, a number or a boolean. */
export type Scalar = string | number | boolean;

## StoredRow  chord/src/store/rows.ts

/** A row as the outbox records it: the stored values, `opt(...)` columns absent when `NULL`. */
export type StoredRow = { readonly [column: string]: Scalar | JsonValue };

	readonly next_id: number;

## Order  chord/src/store/sql.ts

/** An order of rows: the order columns (the key appended as the tie-break) and one direction. */

## Statement  chord/src/store/sql.ts
used by: chord-effect via OwnerTable
/** A statement and its parameters. */
export type Statement = { readonly sql: string; readonly params: SqliteValue[] };

## TableSql  chord/src/store/sql.ts
used by: chord-effect via OwnerTable
/**
 * The statements of one table at one version, rendered once per table handle: the fixed ones as texts, the ones
 * over compiled conditions and `set`s on demand.
 */
export class TableSql {
	readonly table: string
	/** `INSERT OR REPLACE` of a whole row, in `RowCodec.physical`'s order (`put` is an upsert). */
	readonly put: string
	readonly get: string
	readonly delete: string
	constructor(
		table: string,
		columns: readonly Pick<Column, "name" | "type">[],
		physical: readonly string[],
		key: readonly string[],
	)
	/** `SELECT` of `columns` of one row by key: a point lookup, without the `ORDER BY` and `LIMIT` of a page. */
	getColumns(columns: readonly string[]): string
	/** `UPDATE` of one row by key; `versions` gives each `json(...)` column's version to stamp. */
	update(set: SetNode, key: readonly SqliteValue[], versions: ReadonlyMap<string, number>): Statement
	/** `UPDATE` of every row matching `where`. */
	updateWhere(where: WhereNode, set: SetNode, versions: ReadonlyMap<string, number>): Statement
	/** `DELETE` of every row matching `where`. */
	deleteWhere(where: WhereNode): Statement
	/**
	 * A page: rows matching `where` in `order`, after the order values `after` (row-value comparison; the key in the
	 * order makes it total), at most `limit` (bound); every column, or only `columns`.
	 */
	select(
		where: WhereNode | undefined,
		order: Order,
		after: readonly SqliteValue[] | undefined,
		limit: number,
		columns?: readonly string[],
	): Statement
	/** `count(*)` of the rows matching `where`. */
	count(where: WhereNode | undefined): Statement
}

## StagedWrite  chord/src/store/step.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** A write staged for the commit step: its order and what it does there, returning the writes as recorded. */
export type StagedWrite = {
	readonly order: WriteOrder;
	/**
	 * Applies the write inside the step's backend transaction; resolves with the writes as the outbox records them, in
	 * the order applied, with what only the step knows resolved (its seq, a record's revision).
	 */
	apply(step: Step): Promise<readonly StoreWrite[]>;
};

## Step  chord/src/store/step.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * One commit step: its backend transaction, its seq, the store's id allocator (D3: ids are taken from it as the
 * writes apply, never copied), the ids of the documents it created, the table records it changed (the store's catalog
 * takes them after `COMMIT`), the statements it ran (`chord.store.statements`) and the table rows its writes changed
 * (`chord.commit`'s `rows`). Its reads are the step reader of adapters: they see the step's own writes.
 */
export class Step {
	readonly executor: SqliteExecutor
	readonly seq: number
	readonly ids: IdAllocator
	/** The ids of the commit's created documents, in the order of their writes. */
	readonly created: number[]
	/** The table records this step changed, by SQL name. */
	readonly tables: Map<string, TableRecord>
	statements: number
	/** Table rows its writes changed: a `put` one, the others the count their statement returned. */
	rows: number
	constructor(executor: SqliteExecutor, seq: number, ids: IdAllocator, catalog: ReadonlyMap<string, TableRecord>)
	/** Every recorded table as this step leaves it so far. */
	records(): TableRecord[]
	/** The record of table `name` as this step leaves it so far. */
	table(name: string): TableRecord | undefined
	/** Runs one statement. */
	run(sql: string, ...params: SqliteValue[]): Promise<void>
	/** Runs one statement and resolves with the rows it changed. */
	runCounted(sql: string, ...params: SqliteValue[]): Promise<number>
	/** Runs one query for its first row. */
	get<T extends object>(sql: string, ...params: SqliteValue[]): Promise<T | undefined>
	/** Runs one query. */
	all<T extends object>(sql: string, ...params: SqliteValue[]): Promise<T[]>
}

## WriteOrder  chord/src/store/step.ts
used by: chord-effect via StagedWrite
/**
 * Where a staged write goes in its commit: retirements, creations, then everything else, each phase in staging order.
 * A retirement frees a live address before a creation takes it (the partial unique index); an adapter's composite
 * write orders its own parts inside `write`.
 */
export type WriteOrder = "retire" | "create" | "write";

## Attachment  chord/src/store/store.ts
used by: chord-effect via ChordStore
/** What the open host gives the store: its `storage_failed` listener and its batch, in which adapters publish (§1.3). */
export type Attachment = {
	readonly failed: (error: unknown) => void;
	readonly batch: Batch;
};

## ChordStore  chord/src/store/store.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** The store behind `Store`, with what Chord's layers use: commits, guarded reads, the host's failure listener. */
export class ChordStore implements Store {
	/** The claims of its tables and documents (slice 6b). */
	readonly claims: Claims
	/** Its reads by table and its column-set bindings (slice 14). */
	readonly reads: Reads
	constructor(db: SqliteDatabase, meta: MetaRow, catalog: Map<string, TableRecord>)
	get lastSeq(): number
	get outbox(): Outbox | undefined
	onCommitted(listener: (lastSeq: number) => void, onError: (error: unknown) => void): () => void
	/** The allocator's value as the last commit persisted it. */
	get nextId(): number
	/** The id allocator: `mint` takes the next id, `raise` makes room above an explicit one (D3). */
	get ids(): IdAllocator
	/** Takes the next id from the allocator (Durable's `mintId`); refused once the store stopped or closed. */
	mintId(): number
	/** The open host's batch, in which an adapter publishes its commits; `undefined` without a host. */
	get batch(): Batch | undefined
	/** Every recorded table, by SQL name, as of the last commit. */
	get tables(): ReadonlyMap<string, TableRecord>
	export(context: Context): AsyncIterableIterator<ArchivePart>
	/**
	 * Takes the commit queue (an export): resolves once every earlier commit settled, with the release that lets the
	 * later ones run (idempotent). Closing the store calls `end` (from the call on, also while waiting, and at once for a
	 * store closed before the call took the queue), which must release.
	 */
	take(end: () => void): Promise<() => void>
	/**
	 * Resolves once every commit queued before the call settled (stored and adopted, or rejected), also on a stopped or
	 * closed store; commits queued later are not waited for. For a caller that has ended a source of commits and must
	 * not go on while one it queued can still be adopted (the workers component, at a worker's exit).
	 */
	settled(): Promise<void>
	/** The recorded table `name` (its SQL name), as of the last commit. */
	table(name: string): TableRecord | undefined
	/**
	 * The version table `name` is at or is being migrated to: the recorded one, or a higher one a migration announced
	 * before its first commit (`announceTable`), so an old handle is refused before its SQL could queue behind the
	 * migration's DDL (fix round 1, Sol 8).
	 */
	tableVersion(name: string): number | undefined
	/** Announces a migration of table `name` to `version` until the returned withdrawal (after its last commit). */
	announceTable(name: string, version: number): () => void
	/** Attaches the open host; a store attached to an open host is refused (rule 7). */
	attach(attachment: Attachment): void
	/** The host closed: the store may serve another one. */
	detach(): void
	/**
	 * Commits `writes` as one seq when the commit queue reaches it: `fence.admit()` at the entry of its step (its
	 * group's), the writes in their order (retirements, creations, the rest), the outbox commit, `lastSeq` and the
	 * allocator's value, `COMMIT`, then `fence.adopt` before the next step starts. Resolves with the seq. A refused
	 * admission rejects `released`. A step the backend rolled back after the step's own code threw (a refusal, D4)
	 * rejects with that error unchanged and the store goes on; any other failure (`BEGIN`, `COMMIT`, `ROLLBACK`, a
	 * throwing `adopt` or metrics adapter) is an unknown outcome that stops the store (`storage_failed`). `context`
	 * counts the step (no abort once queued).
	 *
	 * Group commit: the commits queued while a step runs form one group, which the next turn admits and writes in one
	 * backend transaction (each commit its own seq, outbox commit and adoption, in queue order; the metadata once), so a
	 * busy store costs a transaction per group, not per commit. If one of them refuses, the group rolls back and its
	 * commits run again one by one as above: the refusal stays its own commit's.
	 */
	commit(writes: readonly StagedWrite[], fence: CommitFence, context: Context): Promise<number>
	/**
	 * Commits `commits` in one backend transaction when the commit queue reaches them, one seq each, in order: each
	 * commit's `check`, which writes nothing, then its writes as `commit` writes them, with its own outbox commit and the
	 * metadata (a commit without writes takes no seq: it stands at the one before). A `check` that throws refuses its
	 * commit: the series stops there and the transaction commits the ones before it. A check whose backend statement
	 * failed, and a throw of a commit's writes, roll the whole series back and reject with that error, the store going
	 * on (D4); any other failure is an unknown outcome that stops the store, as for `commit`. After `COMMIT`,
	 * `receive(index, seq, ids)` is called per stored commit, in order, before the next step starts (`ids`: its created
	 * documents). Resolves with what it stored.
	 */
	commitSeries(
		commits: readonly SeriesCommit[],
		receive: (index: number, seq: number, ids: readonly number[]) => void,
		context: Context,
	): Promise<SeriesResult>
	/**
	 * Runs `read` on the backend under the guard (rule 11, Durable's `GuardedStorage`): refused once the store stopped
	 * or closed; a backend error fails the store unless `context` was aborted (then `aborted`); a read settling after
	 * the store stopped rejects `unavailable/storage_failed`. `read` returns data and never throws for a request: an
	 * adapter checks a request from what it returned, after the guard (slice 6b §1.4).
	 */
	read<T>(read: (executor: SqliteExecutor) => Promise<T>, context: Context): Promise<T>
	/**
	 * `read` for several queries that must see one state (S4, a document from its record and revisions): one backend
	 * transaction, guarded as `read`.
	 */
	readTransaction<T>(read: (executor: SqliteExecutor) => Promise<T>, context: Context): Promise<T>
	/**
	 * Runs `write` on the backend outside the commit queue (the outbox's `trim`), in a backend transaction, guarded as
	 * a read without a context: any error stops the store.
	 */
	async maintain(write: (executor: SqliteExecutor) => Promise<void>): Promise<void>
	close(context: Context): Promise<void>
	/**
	 * Batch apply's turn (slice 6b §1.6, S5): refused (`invalid/args`) while an owner holds a claim (its memory would
	 * go stale) and once the store diverged; otherwise `apply` runs in the commit queue, in one backend transaction, and
	 * returns the position its last commit leaves (`lastSeq`, the allocator's value) and the tables it changed, which
	 * memory takes after `COMMIT`. `apply`'s own error rolls back and rejects as a refusal (a `Diverged` one marks the
	 * store diverged); any other failure stops the store.
	 */
	replay(
		apply: (executor: SqliteExecutor, catalog: ReadonlyMap<string, TableRecord>) => Promise<Replayed>,
		isDivergence: (error: unknown) => boolean,
	): Promise<void>
	/** Whether the store has an outbox, which a replayed batch writes too. */
	get recordsOutbox(): boolean
	/** Throws `unavailable/storage_failed` once the store stopped, `released` once it closed. */
	assertUsable(): void
}

## CommitFence  chord/src/store/store.ts
used by: chord-effect via ChordStore
/** The seal fence's two checks of a commit (§1.3), as the commit step calls them. */
export type CommitFence = {
	/** At the step's entry: `false` rejects the commit `released` and writes nothing. */
	admit(): boolean;
	/**
	 * After `COMMIT`: adopts the commit, `ids` being its created documents' ids in the order of their writes, `rows` the
	 * table rows its writes changed.
	 */
	adopt(seq: number, ids: readonly number[], rows: number): void;
};

used by: chord-effect
/**
 * Opens a store over `backend`: the store's schema migrations, the UTF-8 check, the metadata read once, the outbox
 * switched when asked. A failure closes the backend and rejects (rule 12).
 */
export async function openStore(backend: Backend, context: Context, options: StoreOptions = {}): Promise<Store>

## Replayed  chord/src/store/store.ts
used by: chord-effect via ChordStore
/** Where a replayed batch leaves the store: its last commit's seq and allocator value, the tables it changed. */
export type Replayed = {
	readonly lastSeq: number;
	readonly nextId: number;
	readonly tables: ReadonlyMap<string, TableRecord>;
};

## SeriesCommit  chord/src/store/store.ts
used by: chord-effect
/**
 * One commit of a series (`ChordStore.commitSeries`): its own checks, which write nothing, and its writes. The checks
 * read through the commit's step, which sees what the series' earlier commits wrote.
 */
export type SeriesCommit = {
	/** Throws to refuse the commit: the series stops before it, the commits before it stand. */
	check(step: Step): Promise<void>;
	readonly writes: readonly StagedWrite[];
};

## SeriesResult  chord/src/store/store.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** What a series stored: how many of its commits (`stored`: all of them), and, when one was refused (`refused`), why. */
export type SeriesResult =
	| { readonly kind: "stored"; readonly stored: number }
	| { readonly kind: "refused"; readonly stored: number; readonly refused: unknown };

## Store  chord/src/store/store.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** A store as apps hold it: opened by `openStore`, owned and closed by the app. */
export interface Store {
	/** The seq of the store's last commit (0 for a new store). */
	readonly lastSeq: number;
	/** The outbox the sync layer reads; `undefined` without one. */
	readonly outbox: Outbox | undefined;
	/**
	 * Calls `listener` with the new `lastSeq` after commits are durable and adopted (a commit, a group, a series, an
	 * applied batch): in a microtask of its own, never inside a commit, once for however many commits it covers. A
	 * listener that throws is removed and its error handed to `onError`, never to the commit. Commits a listener makes
	 * are announced like any other. Returns its removal.
	 */
	onCommitted(listener: (lastSeq: number) => void, onError: (error: unknown) => void): () => void;
	/**
	 * The store's state after its `lastSeq` as archive parts (slice 6a §13), holding the commit queue from the first
	 * `next()` until the iteration ends, throws, is closed or `context` aborts.
	 */
	export(context: Context): AsyncIterableIterator<ArchivePart>;
	/**
	 * Closes the store: waits for a running commit step (a group's, its commits' solo runs included), rejects queued
	 * commits and reads `released`, closes the backend. Idempotent, also after `storage_failed`; `context` ends only
	 * this caller's wait (the close goes on).
	 */
	close(context: Context): Promise<void>;
}

## StoreOptions  chord/src/store/store.ts
used by: chord-effect
/** What `openStore` takes besides the backend. */
export type StoreOptions = {
	/** Turns the outbox on (`true`) or off (`false`); omitted, the persisted setting stays (a new store: off). */
	readonly outbox?: boolean;
};

export type AddedColumn = ColumnSchema & (Optional | { readonly default: unknown });

## EvolveOptions  chord/src/store/table-evolve.ts
